299.text: U.S. Census Bureau. Census QuickFacts profile for the city of Huntsville, vintage V2025. Shows the city is more racially diverse, poorer and less insured than Madison County as a whole.

300.title: [18] QuickFacts: Madison city, Alabama (V2025)
300.text: U.S. Census Bureau. Census QuickFacts profile for the city of Madison, vintage V2025. Shows the fastest growth, highest income and largest foreign-born and non-English-speaking shares of the five geographies read.

301.title: [19] QuickFacts: Cullman city, Alabama (V2025)
301.text: U.S. Census Bureau. Census QuickFacts profile for the city of Cullman, vintage V2025. Shows a small, fast-growing county seat with a poverty rate above the county figure.

302.title: [20] County values for Alabama (al_counties.csv; Census QuickFacts V2025 and County Health Rankings 2025 annual release and 25 March 2026 supplement)
302.text: Statewide Alabama Mental Health Systems Report data pack (compiled from U.S. Census Bureau and County Health Rankings & Roadmaps). The already-checked county file from the statewide pack, read from disk rather than re-fetched. It supplies the County Health Rankings measures for Madison and Cullman: provider ratios, uninsured adults, social associations, loneliness, lack of support, children in poverty, severe housing problems and percent rural.

303.title: [21] 310 Boards
303.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH page explaining what a 310 board is and listing the community mental health centers. Establishes that centers are the designated points of entry and are governed by 310 boards, and where Act 310 is codified. The WellStone entry is a bare link with no detail.

304.title: [22] NCAC Impact Report 2025
304.text: National Children's Advocacy Center. The NCAC's impact report for 2025. It gives the founding date, prevention-program counts and the year's revenue and expenditure. Two reads of the intervention-statistics page paired the numbers with different labels, so those figures are not used here.

305.title: [23] About WellStone (wellstone.com/about-us/wellstone/)
305.text: WellStone, Inc.. WellStone's own history page: founded April 1969 as the Huntsville-Madison County Mental Health Board, long known as the Mental Health Center of Madison County, rebranded WellStone Behavioral Health in 2014, merged in 2017 to form WellStone, Inc. Gives undated round figures for employees, clients and facilities. Read once successfully; later wellstone.com pages refused the reader.

306.title: [24] UPDATE: Area's only mental hospital to close
306.text: The News Courier (Athens, Ala.). News Courier report of the announcement, on 13 January 2015, that the state would close North Alabama Regional Hospital in Decatur by 30 June. It gives bed capacity, staff numbers, the Commissioner's statement of what would replace the hospital and the Limestone County probate judge's reaction.

307.title: [25] Mental Health Coalition
307.text: Society of St. Vincent de Paul, Huntsville. St. Vincent de Paul Huntsville's page on the coalition. Confirms from the founding organization's side that its Voice of the Poor Committee formed NAMHC in 2015 and for what purpose.

308.title: [26] Cullman Mental Health Authority to merge with Huntsville's WellStone Behavioral Health Oct. 1
308.text: The Cullman Tribune. Local press report of the merger, effective 1 October 2017, with the combined staff and client numbers claimed at the time and the Cullman executive director's new role as chief operating officer. Older than the time window but the present structure depends on it.

309.title: [27] New jail diversion program addressing mental health, improving recidivism
309.text: WAFF 48. Television report on the Madison County jail diversion program about 90 days after WellStone launched it. It gives the first count of inmates moved out of the jail, the staffing (two case managers), a $70-a-day jail cost figure, and says the North Alabama Mental Health Coalition sought funding from the Huntsville City Council and Madison County Commission.

310.title: [28] Report on Year 1 of Stepping Up Alabama
310.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. Evaluation of the first Stepping Up grant year (October 2018 to September 2019), in which WellStone ran two of the six sites. It gives jail and hospital screening counts for Madison and Cullman counties, case-management follow-up and each site's sustainability position.

311.title: [29] Cullman County Veterans Treatment Court gets underway today
311.text: The Cullman Tribune. Local report on the first session of the Cullman County Veterans Treatment Court on 30 May 2019, presided over by a district judge. It describes the phased supervision model and the first-call court date given on release from the detention center.

312.title: [30] Madison County to launch Assisted Outpatient Treatment program for mental illness
312.text: WHNT News 19. Television news report on the launch of the Madison County Probate Court's assisted outpatient treatment program. Gives the start date (February 3), the partner (WellStone), the funding source (passport application fees) and the steps before a person is placed in the program. The page showed the reader no publication date.

313.title: [31] WellStone to launch mobile mental health crisis response team in Cullman County
313.text: The Cullman Tribune. Cullman Tribune report by W.C. Mann on the planned state-funded mobile crisis team in Cullman County: two-person teams around the clock, pairing a master's-level clinician with a peer or bachelor's-level case manager, with start dependent on hiring. Older than the window; kept because it is the only description of the team's staffing model found.

314.title: [32] Crisis Diversion Centers Awards Announced
314.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH's release naming the first three crisis-center awardees. It names WellStone Behavioral Health in Huntsville and the $18 million appropriation; it names no counties or regions for any center.

315.title: [33] A Work In Progress: WellStone's New Crisis Diversion Center
315.text: Huntsville Business Journal. Report on the crisis diversion center under construction: bed counts at the temporary and permanent sites, the roughly $10 million cost and its funding, including $1 million of American Rescue Plan money from Madison County. It frames the emergency room and jail as the two places a person in crisis otherwise ends up.

316.title: [34] City, WellStone discuss program aimed at improving mental health response
316.text: City of Huntsville. City of Huntsville news release on the council vote backing a co-responder partnership between the City, Huntsville Police and WellStone. It gives the plan (two master's-level clinicians, four 10-hour shifts, 2 p.m. to midnight), the department's monthly mental-health call volume, its count of CIT-certified officers and the 16-hour/40-hour training tiers, and names the CIT coordinator. It does not state a funding amount.

317.title: [35] Cullman County launches mental health court
317.text: The Cullman Tribune. Local report of the announcement by the circuit judge and WellStone. It says applications go through the defendant's attorney or the District Attorney, services are provided by WellStone regardless of ability to pay, and funding is from ADMH and a SAMHSA grant.

318.title: [36] Involuntary commitment law changed in Alabama; taking effect in July
318.text: WAFF 48. Television report on HB70 of 2022, quoting the Madison County probate judge as a supporter 'since day one'. It explains that the law lets an officer transport a person who cannot meet their own needs to a mental health facility to be seen by a physician.

319.title: [37] TAGGS award detail H79SM082921 - Madison County Assisted Outpatient Treatment Program
319.text: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, TAGGS. HHS's award record for SAMHSA's assisted outpatient treatment grant to WellStone, Inc.: project period, funding actions, total and the abstract naming the probate court and Huntsville Hospital as partners, with enrollment and outcome targets.

320.title: [38] The Outlook: Alabama Department of Mental Health Newsletter, Sep/Oct 2022
320.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH's newsletter item on the WellStone crisis center ribbon-cutting of 19 September. It describes the center as a 24/7/365 facility and WellStone as Huntsville's designated 988 call center.

321.title: [39] TAGGS award detail H79SM086485 - WellStone FY2022 CCBHC-PDI
321.text: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Tracking Accountability in Government Grants System. HHS's award record for SAMHSA's 2022 CCBHC planning, development and implementation grant to WellStone, Inc.: project period, every funding action with date and amount, the sum, and the project abstract with its numeric goals.

322.title: [40] City of Huntsville to allocate settlement proceeds to agencies involved in opioid crisis
322.text: WAFF 48. Television news report repeating the City's April 2023 opioid allocation figures. Corroborates the amounts in the City release; adds nothing on the Council vote date.

323.title: [41] WellStone unveils renovation, expansion
323.text: The Cullman Tribune. Local report on WellStone's renovated Cullman site. A WellStone speaker describes separate mobile crisis teams for children and adults in Cullman County, transport to the Huntsville crisis center and the routing of 988 calls to the Huntsville center. Nothing on jail or courts.

324.title: [42] ADMH Board of Trustees meeting minutes, 16 May 2025
324.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. Approved minutes (statewide reference 26). They record that AltaPointe and WellStone were certified by the state as CCBHCs effective July 2024 and that the first demonstration year ends July 2025. They give no numbers served or outcomes.

325.title: [43] Annual Report FY24: Connecting Mind and Wellness
325.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH's FY2024 annual report. Its article on the WellStone pediatric unit gives the opening month, bed count, ages and an average monthly number of young patients to the end of 2024, and says families previously had to travel to Birmingham or Tennessee.

326.title: [44] (Update) Voters reject proposal to increase taxes on local medical cannabis sales
326.text: The Cullman Times. Local press report of the 5 November 2024 referendum result on Cullman County Local Amendment 1, with vote totals. Confirms the proposal, which would have sent a third of the tax to local mental health initiatives, failed.

327.title: [45] Oversight Commission on Alabama Opioid Settlement Funds (ADMH presentation, 22 October 2025)
327.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH's slide deck to the state opioid settlement oversight commission on how the Department used three rounds of appropriations. For this region it shows WellStone won the request for proposals for a 16-bed residential detox program that opened 24 June 2025, and that WellStone received $660,000 as the Region I 988 center under the Round 2 appropriation.

328.title: [46] Alabama Continues Statewide Transition to Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic Model - Expanding into Two New Areas of the State
328.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH release of 28 May 2026 (statewide reference 27). It says Mountain Lakes Behavioral Healthcare (Jackson and Marshall counties) was approved by SAMHSA in October 2025 and Highland Health Systems in April 2026, joining AltaPointe and WellStone, which moved to the model in 2024. It repeats the ability-to-pay rule and says conversion takes six to eighteen months.

329.title: [47] WellStone Expands Access With Mobile Mental Health Unit
329.text: Huntsville Business Journal. Press report on WellStone's mobile mental health clinic, a van that offers therapy and dispenses psychiatric medication, starting at First Stop and the Downtown Rescue Mission, funded by Huntsville Hospital's Community Health Initiative.

330.title: [48] WellStone opens first Madison location, launches upcoming online auction to support local mental health services for area residents
330.text: Huntsville Business Journal (by Katie Holt). Report on WellStone's first clinic in the city of Madison and its spring fundraiser. It carries WellStone's own FY2025 figures for people served and uncompensated care.

331.title: [49] Huntsville Hospital CEO Says Crestwood Medical Center Brand And Operations Will Remain Unchanged After Acquisition
331.text: Huntsville Business Journal. Report of chief executive Jeff Samz's presentation to the Huntsville City Council on 23 April 2026 after the system bought Crestwood Medical Center from Community Health Systems. It gives the completion date (31 March 2026), the system's description of its payer mix and of Blue Cross's market position, and its size. Press report of an executive's statements; no audited figures.

332.title: [50] FY27 Budget Presentation (ADMH, legislative budget hearing)
332.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. The Commissioner's slide deck for the FY2027 budget hearings (statewide reference 30). Slides 26-28 describe the CCBHC model as a Medicaid-reimbursement opportunity and give two access-time results for WellStone between January and December 2025. Only the CCBHC and WellStone slides were re-read for this dossier.

333.title: [51] Inside Alabama's mental health crisis: Two families fighting for change
333.text: WAFF 48. WAFF investigation by Margo Gray quoting the Madison County probate judge and the probate court's director of mental health programs on the commitment process. It is the only source found for the number of involuntary commitments in Madison County (a 2023 peak of 589), the number of beds in the county (60) and the wait for group homes. Families in the story are not named here.

334.title: [52] Statewide pack county table (geo/al_counties.csv): Census QuickFacts V2025, County Health Rankings 2025 annual release and 25 March 2026 supplement, HRSA mental health HPSA detail file
334.text: Compiled for the Alabama Mental Health Systems Report from U.S. Census Bureau, County Health Rankings & Roadmaps and HRSA files. The already-checked county table supplied with the brief (retrieved 3 October 2026). Not re-fetched in this session; values for Madison and Cullman are reproduced as the statewide pack gives them. URL is HRSA's download page for the HPSA file; the County Health Rankings values come from countyhealthrankings.org and the Census values from QuickFacts.

335.title: [53] Cullman Regional Medical Center (member listing)
335.text: Alabama Hospital Association. Alabama Hospital Association listing for Cullman Regional: address, 175 authorized beds and a services list in which the only psychiatric item is 'Psychiatric Outpatient Services'. Supports the reading that Cullman County has no hospital inpatient psychiatric unit.

336.title: [54] Drop-in Centers for Individuals with Mental Illness
336.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH's list of drop-in centers, with addresses and phone numbers. Five are listed statewide; one is in Huntsville and none in Cullman. A companion page (https://mh.alabama.gov/peer-support-drop-in-centers/) defines what a drop-in center is.

337.title: [55] NAMI Alabama Affiliates
337.text: NAMI Alabama. State organization's list of 11 local affiliates. NAMI Madison County is listed; no affiliate is listed for Cullman or for Decatur/Morgan County.

338.title: [56] Wellstone Pediatric Crisis Care Center making great strides, still searching for open positions
338.text: WAFF 48. WAFF news story by Sarah Grace Kennedy, about one month after the pediatric crisis unit opened. It reports that the 24-bed unit could treat only six patients at a time because of a staffing shortage and that 16 patients had been treated since opening. The companion video page (waff.com/video/2024/10/23/...) carries only a one-sentence description saying the same.

339.title: [57] Alabama Comprehensive Provider Manual for Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics (CCBHCs), version 1
339.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. Version 1 of ADMH's CCBHC provider manual (statewide reference 10). It names the payment method (PPS-1, a daily rate per Medicaid beneficiary), says the rate is not paid for people outside Medicaid, sets the 51 percent rule for directly delivered encounters, and requires that veterans be offered help enrolling with the VHA. The current edition (third quarter 2026) could not be read; this earlier edition was used instead.

340.title: [58] Alabama Medicaid 2027 Budget Overview (presentation to the Legislature's budget hearings)
340.text: Alabama Medicaid Agency, via the Legislative Services Agency. The Medicaid commissioner's budget presentation of 29 January 2026, reached on the Legislature's site after the agency's own site refused the reader. It gives enrollment, the share of each county's population eligible in FY2024 (Madison is among the five lowest), spending by category including mental health, and the FY2027 request.

341.title: [59] HUD 2022 Continuum of Care Homeless Assistance Programs Homeless Populations and Subpopulations: AL-503 Huntsville/North Alabama CoC
341.text: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD Exchange). HUD's report of the 22 February 2022 point-in-time count for AL-503. Used for the year-on-year series and the subpopulation counts.

342.title: [60] HUD 2025 Continuum of Care Homeless Assistance Programs Homeless Populations and Subpopulations: AL-503 Huntsville/North Alabama CoC
342.text: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD Exchange). HUD's one-page report of the 28 January 2025 point-in-time count for the AL-503 Continuum of Care. It gives persons and households by emergency shelter, transitional housing and unsheltered, and subpopulation counts including 'Severely Mentally Ill' and 'Chronic Substance Abuse'. It is the latest HUD-published count for the Continuum that contains Madison County.

343.title: [61] HUD 2025 Continuum of Care Homeless Assistance Programs Housing Inventory Count Report: AL-503 Huntsville/North Alabama CoC
343.text: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD Exchange). HUD's 2025 bed inventory for AL-503, with a summary table and a project-by-project list. Read five times in this sweep: the year-round bed totals agree on every read; the project list shows two permanent supportive housing projects, one of them WellStone's.

344.title: [62] An Evaluation of the Alabama Department of Mental Health Crisis Centers (preliminary report)
344.text: Alabama Commission on the Evaluation of Services. State evaluation of the six crisis centers. It publishes no per-center table of admissions, law-enforcement referrals or jail/ED avoidance; for WellStone it gives only the split of spending between operations and capital by year. It finds the centers' monthly data inconsistent and says one center has always reported zero for jail avoidance.

345.title: [63] Huntsville Police co-responder program paying dividends in helping those in crisis
345.text: City of Huntsville (City Blog). City feature on the co-responder program about six months after it began. It confirms the May 2021 council vote to fund it and that two full-time master's-level clinicians ride with CIT officers. It gives anecdotes ('dozens of calls') but no outcome counts.

346.title: [64] Innovative Solutions, Enduring Impact: Annual Report FY25
346.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH's annual report for the year to 30 September 2025. Page 29 lists individuals served by provider in separate tables (community mental health centers, CCBHCs, 988 call centers, crisis centers, child/adolescent mobile crisis teams, state facilities); pages 19-21 give narrative totals for 988 calls and crisis-center evaluations. Read three times in this sweep with differently worded questions; the third read returned the raw text of page 29, in which each table's heading follows its rows.

347.title: [65] Corrections Division
347.text: Madison County Sheriff's Office. Sheriff's Office page giving the detention facility's vision, goals and emergency-response team mission. It publishes no capacity, population, staffing, screening or mental-health information.

348.title: [66] Wellstone Inc - Nonprofit Explorer organization page
348.text: ProPublica (from IRS Form 990 data and Federal Audit Clearinghouse). ProPublica's presentation of IRS Form 990 data and federal single-audit listings for WellStone, Inc. Form 990 figures run from fiscal 2011 to the year ending September 2021; for the years ending September 2022 to 2025 it lists single audits only, with no Form 990 data, and the reader reported the organization flagged as not required to file. The audit documents themselves could not be opened.

349.title: [67] City of Cullman - City Council minutes, 9 March 2026
349.text: City of Cullman. Official council minutes. Record the Council reappointing a member to the WellStone Board of Directors for a term expiring in 2032 - direct evidence of the City of Cullman's appointing role.

350.title: [68] City of Madison, Alabama - City Council agenda packet, 23 October 2023
350.text: City of Madison, Alabama. Council packet containing the FY24 agency appropriation resolutions and agreements. Establishes the City of Madison's FY24 annual appropriation of $45,000 to WellStone (Resolution 2023-337-R) and $15,000 to Crisis Services of North Alabama (Resolution 2023-336-R).

351.title: [69] WellStone Celebrates First Successful Year Of 24/7 Pediatric Emergency Services Unit, Thanks Supporters
351.text: Huntsville Business Journal. News report by Katie Holt on a WellStone event marking the pediatric unit's first year. It gives the number of individuals the unit had served, quotes chief executive Jeremy Blair on how many pediatric patients used to be sent out of Madison County, and reports his announcement that the unit now takes children as young as eight. It gives no funding amounts, lengths of stay or county breakdown.

352.title: [70] Strategic Plans of our 310 Boards
352.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH index page linking each local planning body's strategic plan. For Madison and Cullman it lists three separate plans: WellStone Behavioral Health (Cullman, Madison), the Madison County 310 Board (Madison) and the Cullman County Center for the Developmentally Disabled (Cullman).

353.title: [71] Madison County Four Year Plan for Services for Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities 2026 to 2029
353.text: Madison County 310 Board (filed with ADMH). Plan of the second 310 board in Madison County, which covers intellectual-disability support coordination, not mental illness. States it was established by the City of Huntsville and the Madison County Commission in 1990, names its funders and gives a FY26 cost projection.

354.title: [72] Cullman County 310 Authority Five-Year Plan 2022
354.text: Cullman County 310 Authority / Cullman County Center for the Developmentally Disabled (filed with ADMH). Plan of the Cullman County 310 authority for developmental-disability services, active until 2027. Names local funders (City of Cullman, Cullman County, United Way of Cullman County) and lists unmet needs. No dollar amounts.

355.title: [73] Homeless Resources
355.text: City of Huntsville. The City's homelessness page. It describes the Homeless Services Team, says the Community Development Department leads the partners working through the Continuum of Care, lists partner agencies and links to the AL-503 site and a volunteer form for the South Derrick Street Camp.

356.title: [74] Huntsville City Council approves 2027 fiscal year balanced operating budget
356.text: City of Huntsville. City news release on the adopted FY2027 budget. Gives the General Fund total and the two outside-agency totals. It names no agency and does not mention mental health, opioid funds or homelessness.

357.title: [75] Madison County Commission approves FY27 budget, advances $10 million courthouse renovation
357.text: 256 Today. Press report on the Madison County Commission's FY2027 budget meeting. Gives no budget total and no agency appropriations, but reports the renewed jail health contract with Southern Health Partners, including a mental health nurse paid from opioid settlement funds.

358.title: [76] Mental health care program underway to aid Cullman County inmates
358.text: The Cullman Tribune. Local press report on the Stepping Up Initiative in Cullman County: a $50,000 grant to WellStone, County Commission support and a memorandum of agreement between the Sheriff's Office and WellStone. Older than the time window; no later source on whether it continues was read.

359.title: [77] Cullman County Probate Court (cullmancourts.org)
359.text: Cullman County courts. The Cullman County probate court's page. It names the Judge of Probate and lists 'Commitments' among the court's case types, but publishes no commitment procedure, forms, numbers or holding arrangements.

360.title: [78] Alabama committee continues to hear proposals for use of opioid settlement funds
360.text: The Cullman Times. Press report of a state opioid settlement commission hearing at which the Cullman County sheriff described the lack of facilities to take people needing mental evaluations. No Cullman allocation amounts.

361.title: [79] Madison County probate court launches new program to help with mental health
361.text: WAFF 48. Television news report dated 2 February 2020 on the same program. Gives the program design (case manager and therapist, reporting every 30 days for up to 150 days, assessments at Huntsville Hospital) and the probate judge's statement that over 300 people were involuntarily committed in Madison County the previous year.

362.title: [80] Wellstone, probate judge offer innovative program
362.text: 256 Today. Feature on the Madison County AOT program three years in. It reports the SAMHSA grant to WellStone (four years, nearly $900,000 a year, received December 2022), the use of $35 passport fees to fund two case managers, repeat-petition counts for 2019 and 2021 and a recidivism figure of under 20 percent among completers.

363.title: [81] Judge turns passport fees into mental health care
363.text: The Decatur Daily (state capital coverage). News report on the Madison County probate judge using passport application fees to hire a mental health case worker who follows people after commitment. It gives people served since late 2019 and a recidivism rate. The reader could not extract a publication date or byline, so 'last year' in the article cannot be pinned to a year.

364.title: [82] 'Mental Health Court' for nonviolent offenders launches in Cullman
364.text: The Cullman Times. Local report on the Cullman County Mental Health Court, launched in late May 2022 under the presiding circuit judge with WellStone. It gives eligibility (non-violent defendants who plead guilty), the possibility of dismissal, the funding sources, and notes existing Drug Court and Veterans Court dockets.

365.title: [83] 2025 Community Health Needs Assessment - Cullman County, Alabama
365.text: Cullman Regional Medical Center (prepared by Professional Research Consultants, Inc.). The 2025 CHNA for Cullman County prepared by PRC for Cullman Regional. Mental health is ranked first and substance use second among the prioritized health needs; it reports suicide and overdose death rates, a mental-health-provider rate against the US, and key-informant comments on psychiatrist, nurse and bed shortages. Read through a summarizing reader, so only the quoted passages were confirmed.

366.title: [84] 2025 CHNA Implementation Plan
366.text: Cullman Regional Medical Center. Cullman Regional's implementation strategy for the 2025 CHNA, adopted by its Board of Directors on 11 March 2025. Mental health is one of seven needs selected; the plan cites a Project Zero Suicide partnership, an employed board-certified psychiatrist, a dedicated behavioral health area in the ER and a second licensed counselor in the ER, and lists WellStone as a partner.

367.title: [85] United Way of Madison County website - home page (Community Needs Assessment section)
367.text: United Way of Madison County. United Way's home page, which reports a community needs survey run from 15 May to 30 June 2024 and links the full report and its 2024 annual summary. The linked PDFs could not be read, so the page establishes only that the assessment exists.

368.title: [86] Madison County, AL LIVE UNITED 2024 Community Needs Assessment - Executive Summary
368.text: United Way of Madison County / Alabama A&M University. Executive summary of the 2024 Madison County needs assessment. The three most-named needs are transportation, environmental pollution/recycling and services for abused and neglected children; mental health appears as a recommendation, not as a ranked finding. No mental health statistics are given in the summary.

369.title: [87] With Huntsville center opening, WellStone CEO talks mental health challenges
369.text: 256 Today. Interview-based news story by Kimberly Ballard published days before WellStone's crisis center at 4020 South Memorial Parkway opened. It reports the CEO's statements on workforce supply, reimbursement and pay, the growth from 200 employees in 2011 to 450, and the $10 million cost and funding split of the crisis center. Press report; no primary document for these staffing statements was found.

370.title: [88] New facility responds to mental health emergencies
370.text: Redstone Rocket. Army-post newspaper feature on the opening of WellStone's permanent crisis facility in October 2022 (page date not returned; the text counts 'as of Oct. 12'). It gives bed numbers for the two units, the count served at the temporary site in 2022, the rear entrance for HEMSI and law-enforcement transports, the stated diversion purpose and the funding split.

371.title: [89] Be the Rock (campaign page)
371.text: WellStone, Inc.. WellStone's capital campaign landing page. Says the campaign supports the new crisis center for WellStone Emergency Services and calls it Alabama's first 24/7 crisis center. It publishes no goal, total raised, donor names or public funding amounts.

372.title: [90] Anonymous matching donation boosts WellStone's Pediatric Crisis Care
372.text: Huntsville Business Journal (by Sarah Zupko). Report on a $150,000 matching gift to the Be the Rock campaign in December 2024, with the number of young people served by the pediatric unit to that date.

373.title: [91] The ribbon is cut on WellStone's 24/7 pediatric unit
373.text: WellStone, Inc.. WellStone's own news post on the ribbon-cutting for the WellStone Emergency Services pediatric unit. Gives the unit's size (24 beds, 12,000 square feet), cost ($9 million), funding sources and named clinical leads, and repeats the HEMSI figure of about 800 children transported out of county a year. The date is taken from the URL.

374.title: [92] Madison County, Alabama 2025 Recovery Plan (State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds)
374.text: Madison County Commission (posted by U.S. Department of the Treasury). Madison County's annual ARPA recovery plan report to Treasury. Gives the county's total award and lists a $1,000,000 project for WellStone Behavioral Health under expenditure category 1.12 Mental Health Services, plus a general nonprofit allocation.

375.title: [93] State General Fund Appropriations Comparison Sheet for FY 2027 - SB146 (Act 2026-383)
375.text: Alabama Legislative Services Agency. Enacted General Fund comparison sheet. The mental health earmarks fund crisis diversion centers, civil commitment and children's mobile crisis as statewide lines; no line names WellStone, Huntsville, Madison County, Cullman or the pediatric unit.

376.title: [94] Nonprofit Explorer API record for Wellstone Inc (EIN 63-0579328)
376.text: ProPublica (from IRS Form 990 data). Machine-readable extract of WellStone's Form 990 filings for fiscal years ending September 2011 to September 2021: total revenue, expenses, assets, liabilities, contributions and program revenue. Establishes the financial trajectory through the 2017 merger. No Form 990 data after FY2021 is present.

377.title: [95] WellStone FY21 Annual Report
377.text: WellStone, Inc.. WellStone's published annual report for fiscal year 2021. It is the only WellStone document found that breaks revenue down by federal, state, local government and patient fees, and gives personnel and operating cost. One revenue figure is truncated in the text the reader extracted. No board list or donor list is included.

378.title: [96] TAGGS recipient detail - WELLSTONE, INC.
378.text: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, TAGGS. HHS's list of all its grant actions to WellStone, Inc. (UEI JNLUGFPDX2R5), fiscal years 2021-2025: three SAMHSA awards and a grand total.

379.title: [97] TAGGS award detail H79SM085574 - WellStone FY2021 CMHC Project
379.text: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, TAGGS. HHS's award record for SAMHSA's 2021 Community Mental Health Centers grant to WellStone, Inc.: a two-year project, the original award, a later downward adjustment and the net total, plus the abstract's goals.

380.title: [98] Huntsville City Council approves $343 million operating budget for 2026 fiscal year
380.text: City of Huntsville. The City's own news release on the FY2026 budget adopted 25 September 2025. It gives the operating total, $30,417,499 for 60 outside agencies, and records an amendment moving $36,000 from $900,000 allotted to WellStone to United Cerebral Palsy. The linked budget ordinance packet could not be opened.

381.title: [99] Council approves $330 million municipal budget for FY25
381.text: City of Huntsville. The city's release on its adopted FY2025 budget: the operating total, the total for outside agencies and the council's amendments. It names no amount for WellStone or any behavioral-health agency.

382.title: [100] Cullman City Council approves $58.5M FY2027 budget, discloses 1.3% revenue decrease for FY2026
382.text: The Cullman Tribune. Local report on the City of Cullman's FY2027 budget. It says a resolution authorized community-service contracts with 20 organizations including 'Cullman Area Mental Health (Wellstone)', Cullman Regional Medical Center and Good Samaritan Clinic. No amounts are given.

383.title: [101] Cullman County Commission approves FY 2027 budget, discusses water billing transition
383.text: The Cullman Tribune. Local report on Cullman County's $94,621,043 FY2027 budget. As read it has no line for WellStone, mental health, the hospital, the free clinic or opioid-settlement funds.

384.title: [102] Cullman County Commission agenda, 22 September 2026
384.text: Cullman County Commission. The agenda for the commission meeting that considered the FY2027 budget. It lists the budget item and the jail health contract with Southern Health Partners with its amount; it has no item naming WellStone, mental health or opioid funds.

385.title: [103] Huntsville City Council approves opioid settlement funds
385.text: WHNT News 19. Television news report that the Huntsville City Council unanimously approved the distribution agreements with First Stop, WellStone and the Huntsville Hospital Foundation. It is the only source found confirming the Council vote; no date was shown to the reader and no per-agency amounts are given.

386.title: [104] Huntsville to allocate settlement proceeds to agencies on front lines of opioid crisis
386.text: City of Huntsville. City of Huntsville news release announcing how its first opioid settlement proceeds would be divided among three agencies, pending Council approval. Gives the McKesson and Janssen amounts, the three allocations, the selection rationale and the reporting requirement.

387.title: [105] County allots $250,000 in opioid settlement funds to Good Samaritan clinic
387.text: The Cullman Times. Local press report that the Cullman County Commission amended its FY2024 budget to give $250,000 of opioid settlement money to the Good Samaritan Health Clinic, and that the City of Cullman pledged the same amount from its own share.

388.title: [106] 'This is really going to hurt the patients'
388.text: The Cullman Times. Local press report before the November 2024 referendum on Cullman County Local Amendment 1, a 15 percent local tax on medical cannabis with a third of proceeds earmarked for mental health. Also reports $150,000 of county opioid settlement money approved for the district attorney's drug court over three years.

389.title: [107] City of Cullman - City Council minutes, 22 June 2026
389.text: City of Cullman. Official council minutes. Record Resolution 2026-118, a one-time $125,000 appropriation from the city's opioid recovery funds to Restoring Women Outreach, Inc., passed unanimously.

390.title: [108] Opioid Settlement Grant Program: Round 3 awardees
390.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. List of Round 3 awards by category (prevention, recovery, treatment) with amounts. Read twice; both readings agree on the Cullman and Madison County organizations. Counties served are not shown.

391.title: [109] Annual Report FY21
391.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH's FY2021 annual report. It gives WellStone's FY2021 counts in the provider tables and names WellStone as one of the three original crisis-center awardees and a rural crisis awardee for Cullman.

392.title: [110] Annual Report FY22
392.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH's FY2022 annual report. It gives WellStone's FY2022 counts in the provider tables, the 15-county catchment of the Huntsville crisis center and the $500,000 rural and mobile crisis award to WellStone in Cullman.

393.title: [111] Annual Report FY23
393.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH's FY2023 annual report. It gives WellStone's FY2023 counts in the mental-illness and substance-use provider tables and a mobile-crisis map legend that lists WellStone teams in Cullman County, Madison County and for children and adolescents.

394.title: [112] WellStone Mental Health Update Highlights Planned Expansion To Meet Community Needs
394.text: Huntsville Business Journal. Report of WellStone's 28 March 2024 'Mental Health Update'. It carries the CEO's statement that the jail diversion program saves about $300,000 of taxpayer money a year 'the last time we measured', with no method given, and his remark that the adult crisis center has saved costs for the two Huntsville hospital emergency departments. It also gives HEMSI's out-of-county youth transport figure.

395.title: [113] WellStone opens new mental health clinic in Madison
395.text: Behavioral Healthcare Network (bhnet.org), news item. A trade news site's item on WellStone's new therapy clinic in the city of Madison: location, services, ages served and a quotation from the chief executive.

396.title: [114] First Episode of Psychosis Program
396.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH's page on its three first-episode psychosis sites, one of which is NOVA-Huntsville at WellStone in Madison County. It lists the services offered and a statewide coordinator; it gives no caseload or site contact.

397.title: [115] ADMH Board of Trustees meeting minutes, 21 November 2025
397.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. Signed minutes recording that five more centers will become CCBHCs in 2026, the 988 answer rate and monthly crisis-center evaluations. No provider is named.

398.title: [116] About
398.text: Crisis Services of North Alabama. CSNA's description of its services and the counties each covers. It establishes that CSNA manages 211 for six counties that include Madison but not Cullman, and that its only listed Cullman service is sexual assault forensic examinations.

399.title: [117] WellStone, The Link partner for suicide prevention
399.text: The Cullman Tribune (by Amy Leonard). Report on a suicide-prevention education session by WellStone's outreach team at The Link of Cullman County, with a mobile crisis team member's count of crises attended that summer.

400.title: [118] WellStone Receives Grant To Support Expanded Mental Health And Substance Use Treatment Services
400.text: Huntsville Business Journal. Local business-press report of SAMHSA's September 2022 award of a four-year CCBHC grant to WellStone. It describes what the grant is to fund (24/7/365 crisis care, care coordination, primary health screenings, a mobile crisis team, veterans' services) and quotes the chief executive. It does not give the dollar amount.

401.title: [119] Press Release: WellStone Implements CCBHC Model of Care
401.text: WellStone. WellStone's own release (dated 11 June 2024 by its URL) on Alabama's selection for the CCBHC Medicaid demonstration. It says WellStone and AltaPointe are the first two clinics, that WellStone first received funding in 2022 to adopt the model, and that it has since added primary care and an adult mobile crisis team. It gives no grant amount, no payment-rate detail and no count of people served. The reader returned short quotations only, not the full text.

402.title: [120] Rural Crisis Care and Mobile Crisis Teams
402.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH's page on rural crisis programs and mobile crisis teams, listing funded centers and counties by funding round. In the ring it names only Northwest Alabama Mental Health Center (Marion and Winston); in the core, WellStone (Cullman, and Cullman and Madison for the child/adolescent team). The statewide pack's geo/overlays.json (browser read, 2026-10-03) recorded this page as last modified 2026-09-28; today's reader showed no date on the page.

403.title: [121] Redstone Rocket report on the WellStone pediatric unit ribbon-cutting
403.text: The Redstone Rocket. Report by Marian Accardi on the ribbon-cutting for the WellStone Emergency Services Pediatric Unit. It gives the size, bed count and initial age range (12 to 18), says the unit was expected to open by the end of September 2024, and repeats the figure of over 800 children transported elsewhere for care.

404.title: [122] WellStone unveils new pediatric crisis care center, the first of its kind in the state
404.text: WAFF 48. Television news report by D'Quan Lee on the unveiling (the reader gave 19 September 2024 as the date; the URL path is dated 20 September). It gives 24 beds for ages 12 through 18, an end-of-month opening, the figure of 800 Madison County children a year seeking care outside the county, and a speaker's view that two to three more such facilities are needed.

405.title: [123] ADMH Annual Report FY15/FY16
405.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. The Department's combined annual report for fiscal years 2015 and 2016. Its only reference to North Alabama Regional Hospital is one sentence in the Commissioner's introduction saying the Decatur hospital closed as 2015 closed, leaving all remaining state hospitals in Tuscaloosa; it gives no month, bed count, catchment or replacement plan.

406.title: [124] Behavioral Health
406.text: Huntsville Hospital. Huntsville Hospital's behavioral health page. It describes inpatient programming for adults and seniors and round-the-clock admission assessment in the emergency department, with no bed count and nothing on tele-psychiatry or outpatient care.

407.title: [125] The Health Care Authority of the City of Huntsville - combined financial statements, years ended June 30, 2025 and 2024
407.text: Alabama Department of Examiners of Public Accounts (filed CPA audit). Audited financial statements of the public authority that owns Huntsville Hospital Health System, with the auditor's report dated 21 October 2025. Gives revenue, expenses, charity and uncompensated care, licensed beds by campus including Decatur West's psychiatric beds. Amounts are in thousands of dollars. Payer mix appears only as a graph the reader could not read; the audit firm's name was not returned.

408.title: [126] Unity Psychiatric Care - Huntsville
408.text: Unity Psychiatric Care. The operator's page for its Huntsville hospital. It describes a 20-bed hospital giving inpatient care to people 55 and older at 5315 Millennium Drive NW.

409.title: [127] Crestwood Medical Center (member listing)
409.text: Alabama Hospital Association. Alabama Hospital Association listing for Crestwood Medical Center in Huntsville: address and 180 authorized beds. The reader reported that psychiatric or behavioral health services are not among the services listed on this page.

410.title: [128] Expansion
410.text: Cullman Regional Medical Center. The hospital's page on its building program. It says the emergency department expansion completed in July 2022 includes a dedicated behavioral health treatment area. It mentions no psychiatric beds.

411.title: [129] Alabama Administrative Code r. 410-2-4-.10, Psychiatric Care (State Health Plan)
411.text: State Health Planning and Development Agency, via the Alabama Legislature's administrative code service. The State Health Plan rule on inpatient psychiatric beds, a new rule effective 14 June 2024. It sets a regional bed-need method with three bed categories and occupancy triggers and lists the counties of each planning region. It prints no bed inventory. The county list came back as interleaved columns.

412.title: [130] Provider directory: Madison County (five pages)
412.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH's online provider directory filtered to Madison County, 43 listings over five pages (…/page/2/ to …/page/5/), each with a category: developmental disabilities, substance use disorder, mental illness, crisis center. It is the Department's own list of certified and contracted providers by county; it gives names and phone numbers, not capacity.

413.title: [131] Provider directory: Cullman County (two pages)
413.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH's online provider directory filtered to Cullman County, 13 listings over two pages. The address …/cullman-county/ returns no listings; …/cullman/ returns the 13.

414.title: [132] Bradford Health Services - Madison, AL
414.text: Bradford Health Services. The provider's page for its Madison campus: address, on-site medical detox, residential treatment, medication-assisted treatment and a veterans program. It gives no bed count.

415.title: [133] FY 24 Catchment Area Awardee's (prevention)
415.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health, Office of Prevention. ADMH's list of the organizations awarded substance-use prevention funding for each catchment area in FY2024. WellStone is the awardee for both the Madison and the Cullman catchments.

416.title: [134] Mental Health First Aid equips UAH faculty, staff to support students
416.text: Huntsville Business Journal (staff reports). Report that WellStone's prevention program has taught Mental Health First Aid at the University of Alabama in Huntsville since 2023, with the number of staff trained and the class size.

417.title: [135] NAMI Madison County Alabama (home page; namihuntsville.org redirects here)
417.text: NAMI Madison County Alabama. The local NAMI affiliate's site (namihuntsville.org redirects to it): its classes and support groups, October 2026 meeting dates, address and phone.

418.title: [136] Crisis Services of North Alabama (home page)
418.text: Crisis Services of North Alabama. The organization's home page. It describes the 24-hour HELPline, the HOPE Place emergency domestic-violence shelter, sexual-assault support including forensic exams, and legal advocacy, and states the counties served: domestic violence and sexual assault in Madison, Morgan, Limestone and Jackson, with sexual-assault response in Cullman and Winston.

419.title: [137] Peer Support
419.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH's public page on peer support: who provides it, the statewide warmline, and the two peer-run recovery organizations for substance use with their locations and hours. Huntsville is listed for one of them; Cullman for neither.

420.title: [138] Recovery Support
420.text: Not One More Alabama. The Huntsville nonprofit's own page on its recovery support: referral to treatment, recovery housing and detox, and peer-led sober social events. It gives an address and phone and no counts; it does not mention the Recovery Resource Hub.

421.title: [139] WellStone's new mental health facility opening soon in Huntsville
421.text: WAFF 48. Local television report on the new crisis building: its size, initial bed count, round-the-clock opening and the statement that people leaving are assigned a care manager.

422.title: [140] Fox Army Health Center - Behavioral Health Department
422.text: Defense Health Agency (redstone.tricare.mil). The military clinic's own page for its behavioral health department on Redstone Arsenal: services, who may use it, hours, self-referral and referral off post.

423.title: [141] Fox Army Health Center - Mental Health
423.text: Defense Health Agency (redstone.tricare.mil). The clinic's general mental health page: behavioral health consultants in primary care, the services offered, and where to go in an emergency - 988, the nearest emergency room or WellStone Emergency Services.

424.title: [142] VA Birmingham health care - Locations
424.text: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs. The VA's list of the Birmingham system's sites with addresses. Three are in Huntsville, including one inside Fox Army Health Center; none is in Cullman, Decatur or Madison.

425.title: [143] Huntsville VA Clinic
425.text: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (Birmingham VA Health Care). VA's page for its Huntsville outpatient clinic at 500 Markaview Road NW, part of VA Birmingham health care. It lists mental-health consultation, evaluation and treatment; it is an outpatient clinic with no inpatient care.

426.title: [144] Huntsville Vet Center
426.text: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs. VA's page for the Huntsville Vet Center: address, hours, the counseling it offers at no cost and who is eligible.

427.title: [145] WellStone expands, renovates facility
427.text: The Cullman Times. Press report on the renovated Cullman campus on Commerce Avenue. It names programs run from the building (child and adolescent mobile crisis, outreach, primary care), says it responds to 988 calls in the Cullman area and gives WellStone's combined staff and people-served figures.

428.title: [146] Health Professional Shortage Area Designations
428.text: Alabama Department of Public Health, Office of Primary Care and Rural Health. ADPH's page explaining HPSA designations. It links four maps (mental health and primary care dated May 2024, dental March 2024, MCTAs June 2024) and no list or table; the mental health map is the only ADPH mental-health HPSA document it offers.

429.title: [147] Mental Health Care Health Professional Shortage Areas (HPSAs)
429.text: KFF. KFF's state indicator page built on HRSA data as of 31 December 2025. Used here only for its note on the designation threshold: at least 30,000 residents per psychiatrist, or 20,000 where needs are unusually high.

430.title: [148] 2025 County Data Profiles: Madison County (Alabama Kids Count)
430.text: VOICES for Alabama's Children. The Kids Count county profile for Madison County. It carries a small set of mental health rows: poor mental health days, the population-to-mental-health-provider ratio and the number of children with serious emotional disturbance receiving mental health services in 2024, beside child poverty, insurance and abuse/neglect indicators. Date is the upload month in the URL.

431.title: [149] 2025 County Data Profiles: Cullman County (Alabama Kids Count)
431.text: VOICES for Alabama's Children. County profile from the 2025 Alabama Kids Count Data Book. Re-read twice; the foster care, abuse/neglect and serious-emotional-disturbance rows agreed with the first sweep. The profile prints no source line for these indicators.

432.title: [150] Mental Health Providers (measure description)
432.text: County Health Rankings & Roadmaps, University of Wisconsin Population Health Institute. The measure page for County Health Rankings' mental health provider ratio. It gives the provider types counted, the data source (the NPPES registry of National Provider Identifiers), the data years behind recent releases and the measure's known weaknesses.

433.title: [151] Huntsville Hospital Health System 2023 Report to Our Communities
433.text: Huntsville Hospital Health System. The health system's 2023 annual report. For this dossier it establishes that the system describes Decatur Morgan Hospital West (Morgan County, ring) as north Alabama's only behavioral health hospital with 64 licensed beds, that nurse staffing shortages were its stated top workforce problem, and that it runs in-house training schools. No Madison County psychiatric bed count was found by the reader.

434.title: [152] Psychiatry Residency (UAB Huntsville Regional Medical Campus)
434.text: UAB Heersink School of Medicine. UAB's page for the psychiatry residency based at its Huntsville Regional Medical Campus. It states the program is four years, ACGME approved and accepts up to six residents per year, and lists four faculty. The page gives no start date and does not name WellStone.

435.title: [153] University of Alabama Hospital (Huntsville) Program (Psychiatry), FREIDA program 4000100004
435.text: American Medical Association, FREIDA. AMA residency database entry for the UAB Huntsville psychiatry program: sponsor University of Alabama Hospital, participating site Huntsville Hospital, six positions a year. WellStone is not named.

436.title: [154] Psychiatry Residency: Residents
436.text: UAB Heersink School of Medicine. Lists current residents by class. Only two classes (PGY1 and PGY2) are shown, six in each, which indicates how far the program has filled.

437.title: [155] Psychiatry Residency: Curriculum
437.text: UAB Heersink School of Medicine. Rotation schedule by year for the UAB Huntsville psychiatry residency. It names rotation types (community, addiction, forensic, child and adolescent, geriatric) but no clinical sites.

438.title: [156] Wellstone, Inc. Program (Psychiatry), FREIDA program 4000100008
438.text: American Medical Association, FREIDA. AMA residency database entry for a separate four-year psychiatry program sponsored by Wellstone, Inc. in Huntsville, with its own program number and director. Read twice; it establishes that the WellStone program is a distinct listing from UAB's.

439.title: [157] Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner program
439.text: University of Alabama in Huntsville, College of Nursing. UAH's program page for the PMHNP track. It describes the hybrid format, the 720 clinical hours required and the 1,000 RN hours needed before clinicals. It gives no cohort size, launch date or graduate count.

440.title: [158] Department of Social Work
440.text: Alabama A&M University. Alabama A&M's social work department page, stating that it offers BSW, MSW and PhD degrees. No enrollment, graduate or field-placement numbers are given.

441.title: [159] Department of Psychology and Counseling
441.text: Alabama A&M University. Alabama A&M's psychology and counseling department page. It describes a master's degree in counseling with a clinical rehabilitation counseling specialization and carries a notice to counseling-psychology graduates who have not yet obtained an Alabama LPC. No numbers are given.

442.title: [160] Nursing (Health Division program page)
442.text: Wallace State Community College (Hanceville). Program page for nursing at Wallace State in Hanceville, Cullman County: a practical nursing certificate and an associate degree in nursing, both with continuing ACEN accreditation. It says admissions are limited by faculty and clinical-site capacity; no numbers or pass rates are given on the page.

443.title: [161] Peer Programs
443.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH's peer-programs page describing Certified Peer Specialist and Certified Recovery Support Specialist credentials and listing upcoming training dates. Trainings listed are virtual or at the 4H Center in Columbiana; none is in Madison or Cullman County, and no count of certified peers by county is given.

444.title: [162] Huntsville Police embrace crisis intervention training to help mentally ill
444.text: City of Huntsville (City Blog). City of Huntsville blog post from July 2020 on the police department's CIT training: the requirement rose from eight to 16 hours, WellStone provides several training modules, and HPD was one of four agencies nationally to receive a competitive CIT grant. Older than the report's window but still the only city description of the training content found.

445.title: [163] National Health Service Corps Scholarship and Loan Repayment (ADPH rural health page)
445.text: Alabama Department of Public Health. ADPH's summary of NHSC scholarship and loan repayment: eligible mental health disciplines, the award range tied to HPSA score, and the requirement to serve in a HPSA. No count of NHSC clinicians or sites in the two counties is given.

446.title: [164] Fire & Rescue Department
446.text: City of Huntsville. The department's page: staffing and apparatus. It says nothing about peer support, chaplaincy or behavioral health for firefighters.

447.title: [165] HEMSI home page
447.text: Huntsville Emergency Medical Services, Inc. (HEMSI). Home page of Madison County's ambulance service. It gives headline figures for calls per year, employees and ambulance units. The reader found nothing on psychiatric transports, peer support or naloxone on the page.

448.title: [166] Huntsville Police (main page) and Police Operating Directives
448.text: City of Huntsville. The police department's main page and its directives page (https://www.huntsvilleal.gov/residents/public-safety/huntsville-police/police-operations/police-operating-directives/). Neither describes officer wellness or peer support; the written directives sit in a PowerDMS portal the reader cannot open.

449.title: [167] Wellstone Prioritizing Long-term Mental Health In Children With First Ever Pediatric Center
449.text: Huntsville Business Journal. News report by Noah Logan on the 19 September 2024 ribbon-cutting for the pediatric crisis unit. Gives its size, age range (12 to 18) and maximum stay (14 days), and repeats the figure of nearly 800 children a year transported out of Madison County.

450.title: [168] WellStone home page (navigation, service-location list, patient-portal link)
450.text: WellStone. WellStone's home page as read on 4 October 2026. Its navigation lists eight service locations, a Primary Care service line and a Psychiatry Residency Program page, and its Patient Portal link points to a Netsmart-hosted portal. All deeper wellstone.com pages then refused the reader (robots.txt error), so only the home page and one news post were read.

451.title: [169] Town hall meeting addresses, raises concerns about proposed medical cannabis tax
451.text: The Cullman Tribune. Report of a 29 October 2024 town hall at Wallace State on Cullman County's Local Amendment 1, which would send a third of a 15% medical cannabis tax to the legislative delegation for mental health. WellStone's chief operating officer and a Sheriff's Office captain describe what Cullman lacks. Read twice; the referendum result was not found.

452.title: [170] Huntsville Hospital (member listing)
452.text: Alabama Hospital Association. Alabama Hospital Association listing for Huntsville Hospital: address, 881 authorized beds and a services list that includes a geriatric behavioral health unit and adult, child/adolescent and geriatric psychiatric services. It gives no psychiatric bed count.

453.title: [171] State OKs Madison Street Tower expansion
453.text: Huntsville Hospital. Huntsville Hospital news item on the Certificate of Need Review Board's 20 November 2024 approval of a five-storey, $150 million addition to the Madison Street Tower, taking the hospital from 881 to 931 beds. It does not mention psychiatric or behavioral health beds. An approval and plan, not a completed project.

454.title: [172] Cullman Regional a 175-bed facility with two-phase expansion complete
454.text: The Cullman Times. Hospital-supplied article on the completion of a $30 million expansion that took Cullman Regional to 175 beds. It does not mention behavioral health beds.

455.title: [173] Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics (CCBHCs) Quality Reporting Manual, version 3
455.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH's quality reporting manual for CCBHCs. It sets five clinic-collected and twelve state-collected measures, requires CCBHC electronic health records to be integrated with Alabama One Health Record, sets a 30 September reporting deadline and promises an annual CCBHC Quality Report. These rules bind WellStone as a CCBHC.

456.title: [174] Alabama One Health Record: Alabama's Health Data Interstate (briefing slides)
456.text: Alabama Medicaid Agency / Alabama One Health Record. Slide briefing on the state health information exchange. It gives exchange-wide volumes (46 hospitals sending discharge messages in 2025, 125,000+ providers with access) and shows a governance seat held by Huntsville Hospital Health System, but does not name which Madison or Cullman hospitals or mental health centers are connected.

457.title: [175] North Alabama Coalition for the Homeless website (home page and HMIS page)
457.text: North Alabama Coalition for the Homeless (NACH). NACH's website was under reconstruction when read. Its HMIS page consists of links to a 'ServicePoint LIVE Site' and a 'ServicePoint Training Site', which shows the homeless management information system runs on ServicePoint, but the site publishes no description of participating agencies or data.

458.title: [176] WellStone (service directory entry)
458.text: Alabama Family Central. State family-services directory entry for WellStone. It gives the Cullman phone number and describes the service area as 'Cullman and Decatur Counties', which is not a real county pairing; useful only as an example of directory data quality.

459.title: [177] WellStone Emergency Services Crisis Center (service listing)
459.text: Alabama Family Central. A state-run family services directory's listing for the Huntsville crisis center. It lists the 15 counties but still says the center 'will open for walk-in usage in the Summer of 2022'.

460.title: [178] WellStone still offering School-Based Therapy throughout pandemic
460.text: WZDX / Rocket City Now. Spring 2020 report that WellStone moved school-based therapy to phone and video during school closures, with volumes for 16 March to 17 April. No publication date is shown on the page.

461.title: [179] Community Free Clinic of Huntsville/Madison County (home page)
461.text: Community Free Clinic. Home page of the free clinic at 410 Sivley Road SW: eligibility (uninsured Madison County residents without Medicaid or Medicare), an on-site dispensary and opening hours. No mental health service is listed.

462.title: [180] Partner Programs (funded partners, 1 April 2022 - 31 March 2023)
462.text: United Way of Cullman County. Lists the programs United Way of Cullman County funded in 2022-23 with amounts. The largest award went to the county's developmental disability center; none went to a mental health treatment program.

463.title: [181] Huntsville Hospital's Community Health Initiative
463.text: Huntsville Hospital. Huntsville Hospital's page on its Community Health Initiative grant program for local nonprofits, with 2026 RFP and outcomes-report forms. It says more than $15 million has been invested since 1996 in needs including mental health and medication assistance. It makes no mention of a community health needs assessment.

464.title: [182] Substance Abuse Treatment Services
464.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH's overview of substance use treatment: the number of certified opioid treatment programs and the counties that have them (both Madison and Cullman), and the sliding-fee rule for state-funded providers. Read twice.

465.title: [183] BHG Huntsville Treatment Center
465.text: Behavioral Health Group. Operator's page for an opioid treatment clinic at 4040 Independence Drive NW, Huntsville: hours, medications and payers.

466.title: [184] New Season Treatment Center - Huntsville Metro
466.text: New Season. Operator's page for an opioid treatment clinic at 2227 Drake Ave, Huntsville: hours, medications and payers.

467.title: [185] BHG Cullman Treatment Center
467.text: Behavioral Health Group. Operator's page for the opioid treatment clinic at 1912 Commerce Ave NW, Cullman: hours, medications (including long-acting injectables) and payers.

468.title: [186] Cullman County Detention Facility (provider directory entry)
468.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH provider-directory entry showing that WellStone holds a certified substance-use program site at the Cullman County Sheriff's Office address: Level I adult outpatient treatment, for incarcerated individuals only, funded by ADMH Medicaid, block grant and State Opioid Response.

469.title: [187] Madison County Detention Facility (provider directory entry)
469.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. Directory entry showing that WellStone is the certified provider of adult outpatient substance use treatment at the Madison County jail.

470.title: [188] 2025 Annual Report: Alabama Opioid Overdose and Addiction Council
470.text: Alabama Opioid Overdose and Addiction Council (posted by ADMH). The Council's 2025 annual report. It lists Madison among the counties with the highest Narcan distribution (2,344 doses), reports a 1,278-dose distribution by ROSS in Madison County on Save a Life Day 2025, and describes the statewide mail-order naloxone program run by the Jefferson County Department of Health. The reader found no mention of Cullman County.

471.title: [189] Drug overdose numbers going down in Madison County amid rise in deaths in Alabama
471.text: WAFF 48. WAFF story by Sean Dowling quoting Don Webster of HEMSI on overdose call volume, overdose deaths and Narcan administrations in Madison County in the first half of 2024. The figures are spoken estimates from the ambulance service, not a published dataset.

472.title: [190] Orbit (fixed-route bus)
472.text: City of Huntsville, Parking & Public Transit. The City's page for the Orbit bus: weekday and Saturday hours and fares. No Sunday hours are given; the page metadata shows a 2022 modification date, so it may be out of date.

473.title: [191] Road to Wellness: City transit connects residents seeking mental health care
473.text: City of Huntsville (City Blog). City article on the long-running arrangement by which Huntsville's Access paratransit carries WellStone day-treatment clients: rides a year, dedicated operators, booking, and its origin in the 1990s. Read twice.

474.title: [192] Rural Transportation Resources
474.text: Alabama Department of Public Health, Office of Primary Care and Rural Health. ADPH's county-by-county list of public transport options. It gives hours, booking rules and fares for TRAM and Huntsville Access in Madison County and for CARTS in Cullman County. Undated; the county and city pages themselves could not be opened, so this is the only description read.

475.title: [193] Statewide Rural Transit Study
475.text: Alabama Department of Transportation. Consultant study of Alabama's rural (Section 5311) transit providers for ALDOT. Its provider profiles give operating hours and fleet for the Cullman Area Rural Transportation System and for Transportation for Rural Areas of Madison County (TRAM). The reader found no ridership or funding figures for either.

476.title: [194] Code of Alabama § 22-52-12, Conveyance of person committed to facility; expenses of conveyance
476.text: Justia (2025 Code of Alabama). The statute that governs who takes a committed person to hospital: the probate judge orders 'one or more persons or law enforcement officers' to do it, with expenses taxed as costs of the proceeding.

477.title: [195] Code of Alabama § 22-52-14, Payment of costs
477.text: Justia (2025 Code of Alabama). The statute on who pays commitment costs: the state general fund on the probate judge's order, with exceptions for non-indigent petitioners and respondents.

478.title: [196] Commitment to Mental Institution
478.text: Madison County Probate Judge. The probate court's public instructions for involuntary commitment: where to file, the fee, service by the Sheriff, the guardian ad litem and the appeal window. It says nothing about transport to a hospital.

479.title: [197] Madison County Sheriff's Deputies appointed as mental health officers
479.text: WHNT News 19. Short report of the probate judge appointing Sheriff's Office members as Community Mental Health Officers. It gives their training hours but not how many were appointed.

480.title: [198] Bryce Hospital
480.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH's page on the state's adult psychiatric hospital in Tuscaloosa. It says only that the hospital serves adults throughout the state; no bed count, catchment or admission procedure is given.

481.title: [199] PLACES: Local Data for Better Health
481.text: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. CDC PLACES landing page. It says model-based local estimates are available by county, place, census tract and ZIP Code tabulation area, which makes PLACES the only public source of sub-county mental health estimates for Huntsville, Madison and Cullman.

482.title: [200] Community Health Needs Assessments (web page)
482.text: Cullman Regional Medical Center. Cullman Regional's index of its CHNA reports and implementation plans for 2013, 2016, 2019, 2022 and 2025, with PDF links. Establishes that Cullman County has a published hospital CHNA series on a three-year cycle.

483.title: [201] 2024 Community Needs Assessment: full report (FINALMasterReport_Public-Ver.pdf)
483.text: United Way of Madison County / Alabama A&M University. The full report. It exceeds the reader's 31,457,280-byte limit and failed again; it needs a manual download.

484.title: [202] Huntsville Hospital Community Health Initiative: Request for Proposals, funding year 1 July 2026 - 30 June 2027
484.text: Huntsville Hospital. The hospital's grant call to Madison County nonprofits for 2026-27. It names no priority areas and cites no needs assessment, which bears on whether the hospital publishes its own community health priorities.

485.title: [203] November 2023 Supplemental Report to the 2025 State Health Assessment (community conversations)
485.text: Alabama Department of Public Health. ADPH's supplement reporting community conversations held around the state for the 2025 State Health Assessment. For Huntsville it records the three biggest concerns raised; mental health is not one of them. The reader found no Cullman County session in it.

486.title: [204] Madison County Coroner's Office website (home page and 'About MCCO' page)
486.text: Madison County Coroner's Office. The coroner's office public website. Its pages are Home, About MCCO, About the Coroner, Cremation Permits and Contact; the reader found no statistics, annual report or death counts by cause on the home page or the About page. Establishes that the coroner's suicide and overdose counts reach the public only through news interviews.

487.title: [205] Madison County sees spike of fentanyl and drug overdose deaths
487.text: WHNT News 19. Interview with the Madison County coroner giving overdose counts for June 2021 and the usual monthly average. The page shows no publication date; the text refers to June 2021.

488.title: [206] Madison Co. mental health leaders discuss suicide rates in Alabama as they reach record highs nationwide
488.text: WAFF 48. WAFF story by Sean Dowling in which a WellStone spokesperson relays the Madison County coroner's 2022 suicide frequency and the number of children transported out of the county each year for mental health care. Second-hand figures in a press report.

489.title: [207] Cullman County suicide deaths down in 2022
489.text: The Cullman Tribune (by Amy Leonard). Report giving the county coroner's count of suicide deaths in 2021 and 2022 and WellStone's chief operating officer on the mobile crisis teams.

490.title: [208] Center for Health Statistics (publications landing page)
490.text: Alabama Department of Public Health. Lists ADPH's current vital-statistics publications (113 Causes of Death 2024, County Health Profiles 2023, Alabama Vital Statistics 2023, Vital Statistics at a Glance 2024) and a Statistical Query System for resident births and deaths. No short county-level suicide or overdose table is offered.

491.title: [209] Crisis Intervention Team (Huntsville Police community resources page)
491.text: City of Huntsville. The Police Department's standing CIT page. It states the program's goal and gives a CIT e-mail address and phone numbers. It publishes no officer count, training hours, coordinator name, meeting schedule, co-responder details or statistics.

492.title: [210] Housing Inventory Count & Point-in-Time Count (AL-507)
492.text: Alabama Rural Coalition for the Homeless (ARCH). ARCH's page of its own 2026 count and inventory figures for the 37-county Continuum as a whole. It publishes no county breakdown, so there is no Cullman County figure.

493.title: [211] PLACES county data (data.cdc.gov resource swc5-untb), records for Madison and Cullman counties, Alabama
493.text: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. CDC PLACES model-based county estimates queried through the open-data API for the two counties (four queries: depression and the Health Status category, each county). Gives 2023 estimates of adult depression and frequent mental distress with confidence limits. Other queries used: ...locationname=Madison&measureid=DEPRESSION and ...&data_value_type=Age-adjusted%20prevalence&category=Health%20Status for each county.

494.title: [212] 113 Causes of Death by County of Residence, Race and Sex, 2024
494.text: Alabama Department of Public Health, Center for Health Statistics. ADPH table of deaths by cause, county, race and sex. The reader returned only state totals and the first counties; the contents list shows Cullman County at page 89 and Madison County at page 181, which hold the county counts of suicide and accidental poisoning by race and sex.

495.title: [213] S.A.F.E.R. Together (home page)
495.text: S.A.F.E.R. Together. Site of the firearm-storage suicide prevention initiative for military, veterans and first responders, run with Bearded Warriors, a Huntsville nonprofit, under the Alabama Governor's Challenge.

496.title: [214] The Arc of Madison County (home page)
496.text: The Arc of Madison County, Inc.. Home page of the county's intellectual and developmental disability provider (the first sweep's guessed address did not exist). It gives the mission, people served, address and the program list.

497.title: [215] Regional Autism Network
497.text: University of Alabama in Huntsville, College of Education. UAH page for the Regional Autism Network, an ADMH-funded information hub for 13 north Alabama counties established at UAH in 2018.

498.title: [216] NARCOG (home page)
498.text: North Central Alabama Regional Council of Governments. Re-read for aging services: the home page describes the three-county service area and Medicare (SHIP) help with premiums and prescription costs. Program pages were not linked in the text returned.

499.title: [217] Nonprofit hopes to help fill the void left by the closing of Free2Be
499.text: WHNT News 19. Archived, undated local TV report on the sudden closure of Free2Be, the Huntsville LGBTQ service organization, and on Thrive Alabama's plan to cover part of the gap. Press report; older than the report window, kept because the closure still shapes what exists.

500.title: [218] Thrive Alabama (home page)
500.text: Thrive Alabama. Home page of the Huntsville health center. Lists LGBTQ+ healthcare, HIV care and behavioral health (substance use treatment) with Huntsville, Florence and Albertville sites.

501.title: [219] Rocket City Pride (home page and Resources page)
501.text: Rocket City Pride. The Huntsville pride organization's site (rocketcitypride.com, not the .org address tried in the first sweep) and its Resources page (https://rocketcitypride.com/resources), which lists one counseling practice.

502.title: [220] LIST: LGBTQ+ resources & organizations in North Alabama
502.text: WHNT News 19. Undated Pride Month list of health, mental health and community organizations for LGBTQ+ residents of north Alabama. None is in Cullman County.

503.title: [221] Contact Us
503.text: ¡HICA!. Contact page listing one office, in Birmingham.

504.title: [222] Deaf Services
504.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH page on the Office of Deaf Services. Describes regionally based clinicians and communication-access staff and deaf group homes but names no Huntsville office or staff.

505.title: [223] Counseling Center
505.text: University of Alabama in Huntsville. UAH Counseling Center landing page. Re-read for telehealth: it names Togetherall as an online self-help tool; details sit on sub-pages not read.

506.title: [224] Counseling Services
506.text: Alabama A&M University. Alabama A&M's counseling services page: session length, the concerns addressed, how the service is paid for (through the student health insurance plan, with no out-of-pocket fee) and an after-hours on-call service.

507.title: [225] North Alabama Mental Health Coalition (home page)
507.text: North Alabama Mental Health Coalition. The coalition's public home page. Used only to describe the coalition in its own words.

508.title: [226] About (North Alabama Mental Health Coalition)
508.text: North Alabama Mental Health Coalition. The coalition's own account of its 2015 founding by the St. Vincent de Paul Voice of the Poor Committee, its partners, and the local changes it says it advocated for. Self-description; the claimed achievements need independent confirmation.

509.title: [227] Support Groups
509.text: NAMI Madison County Alabama. The affiliate's support-group schedule: NAMI Connection (peer) and NAMI Family Support Group, with days and places, including a group in Athens/Limestone.

510.title: [228] Not One More Alabama (home page)
510.text: Not One More Alabama. Home page of the Huntsville addiction family-support nonprofit founded in 2016: programs, address and self-description as founded by people with lived experience.

511.title: [229] Partnership for a Drug-Free Community (home page)
511.text: Partnership for a Drug-Free Community. Home page of the Huntsville prevention nonprofit: take-back events since 2010, medication drop boxes, a Recovery Resource Hub with certified peer specialists. The text counts '31 years' and refers to 2020, so it appears not to have been updated since about then.

512.title: [230] North Alabama Walk (Out of the Darkness event page)
512.text: American Foundation for Suicide Prevention. Event page for the 2026 North Alabama Walk at Big Spring Park, Huntsville. No totals or participant counts were shown.

513.title: [231] Peer Support (mental health organizations directory)
513.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH list of peer organizations and recovery community centers. Lists a R.O.S.S. Madison County Community Center in Huntsville; lists nothing in Cullman County.

514.title: [232] Partner Agencies
514.text: United Way of Cullman County. Names United Way of Cullman County's 17 partner agencies. None is a mental health treatment provider; the page gives no descriptions, links or amounts.
