515.title: [233] Mental Health Monday: A look inside Huntsville Police mental illness training
515.text: WZDX / rocketcitynow.com. Undated television feature (the reader found no publication date) on Huntsville Police CIT training with NAMI and WellStone. It describes the 40-hour course of about 26 blocks, the chief's wish for a 16-hour introduction for all officers and a goal of about 30 percent of patrol certified, and names the then CIT coordinator.

516.title: [234] CIT Regional Hubs
516.text: NAMI Alabama CIT Division. NAMI Alabama page listing CIT regions. Region 1 covers 18 north Alabama counties including Madison and Cullman; its training hub is the Huntsville Police Department and its ADMH stabilization center is WES (WellStone Emergency Services). No officer counts.

517.title: [235] Mental Health First Aid
517.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH page on Mental Health First Aid: an 8-hour course, a state contact, NAMI Alabama as a provider and more than 90 certified instructors. No list by city and no count of people trained.

518.title: [236] Mental Health First Aid training to be provided at the Cullman County Library in July
518.text: The Cullman Tribune. Notice of a free two-day Mental Health First Aid course at the Cullman County Public Library in July 2022, presented by WellStone under an ADMH grant.

519.title: [237] Join Us for the UAH x AFSP Out of the Darkness Campus Walk
519.text: University of Alabama in Huntsville. UAH staff announcement of the campus suicide-prevention walk on 27 April 2025 with a fundraising goal above $20,000. An announcement; no result was found.

520.title: [238] Plan to double Alabama's mental health beds, crisis services achievable, budget chair says
520.text: Decatur Daily. Report quoting Rep. Rex Reynolds (R-Hazel Green), chair of the House General Fund budget committee, on paying for ADMH's plan to expand beds and crisis services.

521.title: [239] R.O.S.S. Recovery Organization of Support Specialists (home page)
521.text: R.O.S.S.. Home page of the peer recovery organization: mission, the 24/7 helpline and the places it operates, including Madison County.

522.title: [240] Meet the Judge
522.text: Madison County Probate Judge. Official biography of the probate judge. It records his seat on a Community Advisory Committee for WellStone and his mental health committee work for the state probate judges' association.

523.title: [241] Child and Family Services Resource Directory
523.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH's directory of child and family service providers (the date is the upload month in the URL). The reader returned only the WellStone entries: the main listing for Madison and Cullman counties and a substance-use listing for WellStone's Nova Center on Golf Road. Program-level detail was not returned.

524.title: [242] WellStone (provider directory entry, Cullman)
524.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH's provider-directory entry for WellStone's Cullman location. It lists the services certified there, including child and adolescent case management and outpatient, a juvenile court liaison, 'OUR Kids' in-home intervention and the school-based mental health collaboration.

525.title: [243] WellStone breaks ground on inpatient Mental Health Center for Children
525.text: WHNT News 19. Report on the groundbreaking for the pediatric unit; the reader returned no date or byline. It says the 24-bed, 12,000-square-foot facility was scheduled for completion in 2024, that HEMSI transports more than 800 children a year out of Madison County with about half going to Decatur West, and that patients can wait hours or days for a bed.

526.title: [244] Madison County Schools (home page)
526.text: Madison County School System. District home page. Gives the district's own enrollment statement and links to its counseling, mental health, crisis resources and school safety pages.

527.title: [245] Mental Health Services
527.text: Madison County Schools. Madison County Schools' mental health page. It names the district's Mental Health Services Coordinator, describes a three-tiered model with school social workers and counselors, suicide prevention training and a district suicide protocol, and lists three community partners. It gives no staff numbers.

528.title: [246] Mental Health Matters / Mental Health in MCS
528.text: Madison City Schools. Madison City Schools' page on its mental health supports. It says school-based therapists come from The Enrichment Center, names the district's other community partners and its staff roles, and says suicide prevention training is required for all employees. It gives no numbers.

529.title: [247] The Enrichment Center (home page)
529.text: The Enrichment Center. Home page of a Huntsville nonprofit that provides school-based mental health therapy in three school districts at no cost to families. It gives its own counts of therapists, students and therapy sessions for the 2025-26 school year. It does not name the districts or its funders.

530.title: [248] Mental health resources available for students in Madison County
530.text: WAFF 48. Back-to-school report by Matthew King quoting WellStone's director of development, Karen Petersen. It gives a count of how many times WellStone therapists served Madison County students in fiscal year 2024 and lists school-based therapists, the pediatric crisis unit and emergency services. It names no districts or staffing.

531.title: [249] Huntsville City Schools (home page)
531.text: Huntsville City Schools. The district's home page, read for its enrollment statement and links to its counseling, prevention and support, student welfare and safety pages (those pages could not then be read).

532.title: [250] Huntsville City Schools department pages (Prevention & Support Services, School Counseling, Student Welfare)
532.text: Huntsville City Schools. Three district department pages from the retry list. Each loaded but returned only navigation menus to the reader, with no body text on counselors, social workers, mental health partners or student numbers.

533.title: [251] Mental Health Services
533.text: Cullman City Schools. Cullman City Schools' mental health services page. It names the district's Mental Health Specialist, a licensed marriage and family therapy associate serving kindergarten to grade 12, states the written opt-in rule for students under sixteen, and describes a Peer Helpers program. It does not mention WellStone.

534.title: [252] Cullman City Schools mental health pages (department index, Program Initiatives, Community Resources)
534.text: Cullman City Schools. The district's mental health section. The index returns navigation only (eight sub-pages); the Program Initiatives page lists three external programs; the Community Resources page links to a spreadsheet the reader could not open.

535.title: [253] Cullman Co. Schools receive donation for mental health services
535.text: WBRC 6. Report on a $10,000 donation from the Stephen K. Griffith Memorial Fund to Cullman County Schools for student and family mental health treatment. It names the district's Mental Health Services Coordinator and gives its number of social workers. Older than 2023.

536.title: [254] Mental Health Opt-In
536.text: Madison County Schools. Madison County Schools' page explaining the parental opt-in consent for school mental health services, completed through the PowerSchool parent portal. As read it still states the age threshold as under 14.

537.title: [255] School-Based Mental Health Collaboration
537.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH's page on the school-based collaboration, giving the number of school systems and centers taking part. The linked list of which systems partner with which center returned a 404 error.

538.title: [256] 2025 Alabama Kids Count: Alabama profile
538.text: VOICES for Alabama's Children. State profile in the same layout as the county profiles. Supplies the state comparison values for foster care, abuse/neglect, children with serious emotional disturbance served, the mental health provider ratio, protective services, preventable teen deaths and youth incarcerations. Read once.

539.title: [257] NCAC 2024 Impact Report
539.text: National Children's Advocacy Center. The NCAC's impact report for 2024, with labeled counts of team case reviews, forensic interviews, therapy sessions and intakes, forensic medical exams, family-advocate interactions, school programs and home visits, plus revenue and expenditure. The publication year is inferred from the report year.

540.title: [258] Huntsville/Madison Co. Services
540.text: National Children's Advocacy Center. The NCAC's page for its local services: forensic interviews, a multidisciplinary team (District Attorney, law enforcement, DHR, therapists, medical professionals including Crisis Services of North Alabama), medical exams, trauma therapy to age 18 and family advocacy. No counts.

541.title: [259] What we do
541.text: Brooks' Place Child Advocacy Center (Cullman). Service page of Cullman's child advocacy center: forensic interviews, individual and family counseling, juvenile sex offender management, medical exams, community education and training, at no cost to families. It gives no counts of children served.

542.title: [260] Who we are
542.text: Brooks' Place Child Advocacy Center (Cullman). Brooks' Place's page giving its mission, address, staff (an executive director, a forensic interviewer, a family and medical advocate and two therapists) and its statement that all funding comes from local donations. It gives no founding year, accreditation or numbers served.

543.title: [261] Davidson Farms
543.text: Kids to Love Foundation. Kids to Love's page on Davidson Farms, a home for girls licensed by the state in August 2017 and privately funded, and on its Cottage Community for young women who have aged out of foster care. It gives no capacity.

544.title: [262] Smith Family Wellness Center (hopefortrauma.org)
544.text: Kids to Love Foundation. Site of Kids to Love's trauma therapy service. It lists the therapies offered to children and adults, the insurance accepted (including Alabama Medicaid and ALL Kids), sliding-scale options and locations in Madison, Tuscumbia and Ardmore.

545.title: [263] Childhaven, Inc. (site)
545.text: Childhaven, Inc. (Cullman). Childhaven's own site. It lists its residential, transitional living, foster care and independent living programs, states its capacity and names its executive director. The page is undated and gives no founding year.

546.title: [264] Juvenile Court Ordered Diversion Programs
546.text: Madison County Commission. Madison County's page on juvenile court diversion. It names three specialty courts (Drug Court, Alternative Court, Truancy Court) and describes them as judicially supervised treatment programs for nonviolent offenders involving substance abuse and mental health treatment. It gives no providers, eligibility rules or numbers.

547.title: [265] Hon. Ruth Ann Hall, Circuit Judge (biography page)
547.text: 23rd Judicial Circuit of Alabama (Madison County). The court's biography page for a Madison County circuit judge. It credits her with presiding over the Adult Mental Health Court and the Juvenile Conference Committee, founding the Juvenile Alternative Court and establishing a Veterans Court.

548.title: [266] Neaves-Davis Center for Children
548.text: Madison County Commission. Madison County's page on its juvenile detention facility. It gives the bed count, the facility's purpose, its licensing by the Department of Youth Services and its annual audits. It says nothing about medical, education or mental health services for detained youth.

549.title: [267] 2026 Diversion Grant & Our KIDS Grant Contracts Reference Book
549.text: Alabama Department of Youth Services. DYS's September 2026 reference book describing each diversion grant and Our Kids grant: who it serves, what it provides, capacity, counties and a contact. It gives no grant amounts. Read for the Madison and Cullman entries and for programs whose county lists include them.

550.title: [268] Commission gives CR 222 update, approves renaming of juvenile detention center in honor of Chaney
550.text: The Cullman Tribune. Report of a Cullman County Commission meeting that renamed the Cullman County Juvenile Detention Center. It establishes that the county has a juvenile detention facility of its own.

551.title: [269] Cullman commission approves purchase of new CCSO radios, enters detention agreement with Walker Co.
551.text: The Cullman Tribune. Report of a 2019 commission meeting. The chief of Cullman Juvenile Probation describes the county's 'short-term detention facility' for juveniles and a six-month reciprocal arrangement with Walker County.

552.title: [270] Detention Centers
552.text: Alabama Department of Youth Services. DYS's list of eleven juvenile detention centers with capacities. Re-read to check for a Cullman County facility: there is none on the list. The nearest listed centers are Neaves-Davis in Huntsville (48) and Tennessee Valley in Tuscumbia (25).

553.title: [271] Infant and Early Childhood Special Programs
553.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH's page on infant and early childhood mental health consultation, PATHS and PPEER. It names the state coordinator and links a provider-search dashboard but does not say how many consultants there are or which counties each serves.

554.title: [272] Support Groups
554.text: Huntsville Hospital for Women & Children. The hospital's list of support groups: breastfeeding mothers, children's grief, bereaved parents and a breast cancer wellness program. No postpartum or perinatal mood group is listed.

555.title: [273] Pediatric ER
555.text: Huntsville Hospital for Women & Children. The hospital's page on its pediatric emergency department. It gives annual visits, staffing and its claim to be the only dedicated pediatric emergency service in North Alabama. It does not mention behavioral health.

556.title: [274] Pediatric Care
556.text: Huntsville Hospital Health System. The health system's pediatric care page. Among the conditions its pediatric providers address it lists ADHD, autism spectrum disorder, depression and developmental delays; it lists the pediatric ER, pediatric ICU and neonatal ICU. It lists no psychiatry or psychology service and no bed count.

557.title: [275] Psychiatry (UAB Medicine Huntsville)
557.text: UAB Medicine Huntsville. Clinic page for the UAB psychiatry clinic at 301 Governors Drive SW, Huntsville. It says the clinic serves adults, children and adolescents, does not discharge patients to adult services at 18, and lists four psychiatrists.

558.title: [276] Huntsville Child Psychiatry (practice home page)
558.text: Huntsville Child Psychiatry. Home page of a private child and adolescent psychiatry practice at 101 Lowe Avenue, Huntsville, with one board-certified child psychiatrist. It states that the practice is at capacity and not adding to its waitlist.

559.title: [277] Bridging the Mental Health Gap for Children in Alabama
559.text: Inside Pediatrics (Children's of Alabama). Children's of Alabama article on PATHS. It gives no enrollment counts or psychiatrist numbers; its one quantitative statement is a three-to-six-month wait to see a therapist or psychiatrist.

560.title: [278] Autism Clinic (PAAD Clinic)
560.text: The Arc of Madison County. The Arc of Madison County's page for its autism diagnostic clinic for children aged 2 to 5. It is the only local source found that publishes a waiting time for autism evaluation.

561.title: [279] Resource Guide: ADMH Autism Services (Region I)
561.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. An ADMH autism resource guide compiled by a University of Alabama student intern (the date is the upload month in the URL; the document itself is undated). For north Alabama it lists diagnostic providers, ABA, therapy, residential, psychiatry, counseling, school and support resources with addresses and phone numbers. It is a list of names, without capacity or waiting times.

562.title: [280] County Office Contact
562.text: Alabama Department of Human Resources. DHR's directory of county offices, giving the director, address and phone number for the Madison County and Cullman County departments.

563.title: [281] Huntsville Police Department gives insight into Crisis Intervention Training efforts
563.text: WHNT News 19. Television report (page date not returned; context places it about a year after the 2021 city funding) of a Huntsville Police briefing to the Police Citizens Advisory Council. It gives counts of officers through the 16-hour and 40-hour CIT courses, an annual call figure and WellStone's statement that a federal grant added two co-responders to the two the City funds.

564.title: [282] Huntsville Police Department: 2025 Rewind
564.text: City of Huntsville (City Blog). The City's review of the police department's year. It does not mention the co-responder program, the Crisis Intervention Team, mental health or WellStone.

565.title: [283] Former Huntsville officer pleads guilty to manslaughter in 2018 death
565.text: WAFF 48. Television report of the 13 October 2023 guilty plea to manslaughter by a former Huntsville police officer for a 2018 on-duty shooting of a man who was holding a gun to his own head. It gives the earlier conviction and sentence dates and the plea terms (three years' probation; a 20-year split sentence that takes effect only on violation).

566.title: [284] Alabama Court of Criminal Appeals reverses conviction of former Huntsville PD officer
566.text: WAFF 48. Television report that on 24 March 2023 the Alabama Court of Criminal Appeals reversed the officer's 2021 murder conviction because the jury was instructed on self-defense as it applies to an ordinary citizen rather than a police officer.

567.title: [285] Patrol Division
567.text: Madison County Sheriff's Office. The Sheriff's Office page for its patrol division: sworn strength, area, shifts, K-9 and SWAT. It does not mention crisis intervention training, mental-health deputies or a co-responder.

568.title: [286] Cullman County Sheriff's Office (home page)
568.text: Cullman County Sheriff's Office. Home page and navigation of the Sheriff's Office site. No page or text on mental health, crisis intervention training, a co-responder or WellStone.

569.title: [287] Detention Services (Huntsville Police records pages)
569.text: City of Huntsville. City page stating that detention for Huntsville is managed by the Madison County Sheriff's Office at the Madison County Metro Jail, 815 Wheeler Avenue, and that juveniles are held at the Neaves-Davis Center. It gives no capacity or health-care information.

570.title: [288] Office of Alternative Sentencing (department page)
570.text: Madison County Commission. The department's main page, with a one-sentence description of each program, the office address (715-C Wheeler Avenue, Huntsville) and its director. No caseload numbers are published.

571.title: [289] Municipal Judge says Huntsville court system works to help citizens
571.text: City of Huntsville (City Blog). City feature quoting a Municipal Court judge. It is the only City source found that says the Municipal Court runs its own Mental Health Court and Pretrial Diversion, and that it is tailoring programs for veterans and unhoused people; it also gives the court's caseload and number of judges.

572.title: [290] Report on Year 3 of Stepping Up Alabama
572.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. Evaluation of the third grant year (1 October 2020 to 30 September 2021), covering nine sites including 'Wellstone - Cullman' and 'Wellstone - Madison'. It gives jail-table rows for both and says no site summary was completed for WellStone-Madison because of staff turnover and inconsistent data. Table values were read through the fetch tool and should be checked against the PDF before publication.

573.title: [291] 6 months in, Stepping Up Initiative connecting mental health patients with needed resources
573.text: The Cullman Tribune. Local report on WellStone's Stepping Up work in Cullman County about six months in. WellStone's chief operating officer explains that screening inside the jail failed because inmates declined, and that the program was moving to the courts; it gives the count evaluated at Cullman Regional.

574.title: [292] Huntsville-Madison County Metro jail almost at capacity
574.text: WAFF 48. A 2010 television report in which the then sheriff gives the jail's capacity and population. It is sixteen years old and is recorded only because no current figure is published.

575.title: [293] Meet the Warden
575.text: Cullman County Sheriff's Office. The Sheriff's Office page on the detention center's warden, which carries the only published description of the Cullman County Detention Center found: bed count, opening date, whom it holds, staffing and the work-release program.

576.title: [294] Cullman County Commission approves FY 2026-2027 budget, discusses water billing transition
576.text: The Cullman Tribune. Report of the commission's September 2026 meeting: the FY2027 budget total and the FY2027 Southern Health Partners agreement.

577.title: [295] Lawsuits: Alabama Jailers Allowed 3 Inmates to Die of 19th-Century Ailments
577.text: Mother Jones. Magazine report on three federal suits filed in October 2014 over deaths in Madison County custody in 2013. It sets out the allegations (delay in hospital transfer to save money), the defendants (the county, the then sheriff, the contractor, officers and clinicians), the claims (Fourteenth Amendment, deliberate indifference) and the defendants' denial in court filings.

578.title: [296] Advanced Correctional Healthcare's Business Model Blamed for Prisoner Deaths, Injuries
578.text: Prison Legal News. Trade-press survey of litigation against the jail health contractor Advanced Correctional Healthcare. For Madison County, Alabama it gives the three federal case captions and numbers arising from 2013 deaths and says all three were pending in September 2016. It gives no outcome.

579.title: [297] Elliott v. Madison County, Alabama, et al., No. 5:14-cv-1309-CLS (N.D. Ala.), memorandum opinion and order of 9 March 2015
579.text: United States District Court, Northern District of Alabama (via govinfo.gov). The district court's ruling on four motions to dismiss the second amended complaint in one of the three suits over 2013 deaths in the Madison County jail. All motions were denied and discovery was ordered to proceed. It is a ruling on the pleadings, not a finding of fact; the case's final disposition is not in this document.

580.title: [298] Jail Information
580.text: Madison County Sheriff's Office. Sheriff's Office page for the Madison County Detention Facility, 815 Wheeler Avenue, Huntsville. It names Southern Health Partners as the health-care provider approved by the County Commission. It gives no capacity, population or mental-health service details.

581.title: [299] Hon. Patricia Dunn Demos, District Judge (biography page)
581.text: 23rd Judicial Circuit of Alabama (Madison County). The court's biography page for a Madison County district judge. It states that she was appointed in February 2015 and began presiding over the Adult Mental Health Court of Madison County in 2015.

582.title: [300] Office of Alternative Sentencing & Release (staff and program page)
582.text: Madison County Commission. County page listing the office's programs and a staff directory. Establishes that Madison County's pretrial release, community corrections, probation, court referral, DUI diversion and adult drug court functions sit in one county office, which also runs a Mental Health Pre-Trial Release Program.

583.title: [301] Circuit Court (Cullman County courts website)
583.text: 32nd Judicial Circuit of Alabama. The circuit court's page for the 32nd Judicial Circuit (all of Cullman County). It names two circuit judges and describes jurisdiction. It does not mention the Drug, Veterans or Mental Health Court dockets, community corrections or pretrial services.

584.title: [302] Stepping Up 2026 (county map)
584.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. One-page map with the legend 'Current Stepping Up Counties (48)' and 'Counties without Stepping Up (19)'. The reader's assignment of individual counties (it placed Madison among current counties and Cullman among those without) is not reliable because the PDF text does not cleanly separate the two lists.

585.title: [303] Alabama promised to improve psychiatric care for men charged with crimes. They still wait years
585.text: Associated Press via WSFA. AP report on the Taylor Hardin waitlist under the 2018 consent decree. It gives state figures only and names no north Alabama county; used here to record that no county-level wait data were found.

586.title: [304] Second chance: The Link of Cullman County gears up for program to stop returns to prison
586.text: The Cullman Tribune. Report of a $500,000 federal Second Chance Act grant to The Link of Cullman County for an adult reentry program.

587.title: [305] Mentors needed for The Link's ONE-Eighty program
587.text: The Cullman Tribune. Follow-up report on the reentry program, named ONE-Eighty, shortly before enrollment began in October 2020; names the Sheriff's Office and the Bureau of Pardons and Paroles as partners.

588.title: [306] Day Reporting Centers
588.text: Alabama Bureau of Pardons and Paroles. The Bureau's description of Day Reporting Centers: who they serve, what they address and where they are. Huntsville is one of the five full centers.

589.title: [307] 2023 Alabama Community Corrections Program by County as of April 1, 2023 (map)
589.text: Alabama Department of Corrections. ADOC's county map of community corrections programs with an ADOC contract. It labels Madison as a program organized as an Authority for the 23rd Judicial Circuit and Cullman as a non-profit program for the 32nd Judicial Circuit. The reader's list of counties without a program was longer than the map's stated total, so only the two county labels and the totals are used.

590.title: [308] Community Corrections Program and CCP Directory
590.text: Alabama Department of Corrections. ADOC's description of the Community Corrections Program and its directory of local programs. The directory as returned by the reader was truncated (it stopped at Escambia County), so the Cullman County entry could be read but Madison County's could not be confirmed either way.

591.title: [309] Victim Services announces new name: The Willow Path
591.text: The Cullman Tribune. Report of the renaming of Victim Services of Cullman as The Willow Path from 26 September 2025, with the organization's own description of its services.

592.title: [310] The Willow Path celebrating 35 years
592.text: The Cullman Tribune. Feature on Cullman County's domestic violence agency, formerly Victim Services of Cullman: its shelter capacity, crisis-call volume and year-on-year changes in people served.

593.title: [311] Alabama's Continuum of Care Groups (contact list)
593.text: Alabama Department of Economic and Community Affairs (ADECA). ADECA's contact list of Alabama's Continuums of Care. It names NACH as AL-503 serving Madison, Limestone and Morgan counties and the Alabama Rural Coalition for the Homeless as AL-507 covering the balance of the state; it does not list Cullman County by name.

594.title: [312] About the CoC (Alabama Balance of State CoC, AL-507)
594.text: Alabama Rural Coalition for the Homeless (ARCH). ARCH's description of the Balance of State Continuum of Care with its list of 37 counties. It establishes that Cullman County is in AL-507, not in NACH's AL-503.

595.title: [313] HUD 2023 Continuum of Care Homeless Assistance Programs Homeless Populations and Subpopulations: AL-503 Huntsville/North Alabama CoC
595.text: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD Exchange). HUD's report of the 25 January 2023 point-in-time count for AL-503. Used for the year-on-year series and the subpopulation counts.

596.title: [314] HUD 2024 Continuum of Care Homeless Assistance Programs Homeless Populations and Subpopulations: AL-503 Huntsville/North Alabama CoC
596.text: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD Exchange). HUD's report of the 23 January 2024 point-in-time count for AL-503, with the same tables as the 2025 report. Used for the year-on-year series.

597.title: [315] Point-In-Time Count
597.text: North Alabama Coalition for the Homeless. NACH's page explaining the point-in-time count and linking report files by year. The newest year linked is 2024; the page itself states no totals.

598.title: [316] HUD 2022 CoC Housing Inventory Count report: AL-503 Huntsville/North Alabama CoC
598.text: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD Exchange). HUD's 2022 bed inventory for AL-503, not read in the first sweep. It shows 334 permanent supportive housing beds, 268 of them in a Veterans Affairs VASH project, against 154 the following year.

599.title: [317] HUD's 2024 Continuum of Care Program Funding Awards: AL-503 Huntsville/North Alabama CoC
599.text: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD Exchange). HUD's list of FY2024 Continuum of Care awards for AL-503: four renewal or planning grants totaling $945,663, to the Huntsville Housing Authority, Family Services Center and the City of Huntsville. Read twice with matching results.

600.title: [318] South Derrick Street Camp improvements enhance safety and security
600.text: City of Huntsville. City news release on rebuilding the South Derrick Street Camp after a 2024 fire: an asphalt pad, 84 individual spaces, tents on platforms, a perimeter fence and registration under new community standards. It establishes that the City's Community Development Department manages the camp.

601.title: [319] Homeless camps spreading across Madison County; advocates launch mapping program
601.text: WAFF 48. Press report that First Stop is mapping encampments across Madison County and tracking about 20, with the Derrick Street camp below capacity. It is the only source found for the number of encampments.

602.title: [320] Huntsville refocuses on homelessness
602.text: Axios Huntsville. Press report of the City's 2 June 2026 media roundtable on its Homeless Services Team: 22 former South Derrick Street residents housed in six months, camp occupancy against capacity, and an estimate of about 575 unhoused people. No City document with these figures was found, so this and WAFF are the sources.

603.title: [321] Huntsville says new Homeless Services Team helped house 22 people after Derrick Street reset
603.text: WAFF 48. Press report of the same roundtable, naming the City's first Homeless Resource Specialist and the partner organizations, including WellStone and the police Community Outreach Unit. It corroborates the Axios figure of 22 people housed.

604.title: [322] North Alabama Coalition for the Homeless (home page)
604.text: North Alabama Coalition for the Homeless (NACH). NACH's home page: its statement of purpose, which names substance use and mental health challenges as a focus, and the place and hours of in-person coordinated entry. It does not state the counties served or its Continuum of Care role.

605.title: [323] HUD 2025 CoC Housing Inventory Count report: AL-507 Alabama Balance of State CoC
605.text: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD Exchange). HUD's 2025 bed inventory for the 37-county Balance of State Continuum that contains Cullman County. Its project list includes a 21-bed emergency shelter run by Victim Services of Cullman; the report lists no permanent supportive housing project.

606.title: [324] Warming stations: What you need to know
606.text: The Cullman Tribune. Press explainer on cold-weather shelter in Cullman: the City opens a senior center as a warming shelter at a forecast of 28°F or below, and the county EMA coordinates churches and volunteers. It shows that overnight shelter in Cullman is weather-triggered and volunteer-run.

607.title: [325] HCV/Section 8 Program
607.text: Cullman Housing Authority. The authority's voucher page: jurisdiction is Cullman County, the waiting list is closed, waits can run to months or years. No voucher count.

608.title: [326] Out of Reach 2026: Alabama
608.text: National Low Income Housing Coalition (NLIHC). NLIHC's 2026 state page with fair market rents, housing wages and renter counts for Alabama, the Huntsville MSA and Cullman County. It is the source for what a full-time worker must earn to afford a two-bedroom rental in each place.

609.title: [327] 2024 Strategic Plan
609.text: Huntsville Housing Authority. The authority's strategic plan page. It states that HHA has over 1500 rental units and assists close to 1800 families with Section 8 vouchers, and lists capital spending; it sets no goal on homelessness or supportive housing.

610.title: [328] About Us
610.text: Huntsville Housing Authority. The housing authority's own description: almost 3,000 units of public and other assisted housing, its executive director and mission. The home page adds a 6-to-12-month public housing wait; voucher numbers are not clearly stated.

611.title: [329] Unemployment Rate in Madison County, AL (ALMADI9URN), monthly
611.text: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED); source U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. FRED's copy of the BLS Local Area Unemployment Statistics monthly series for Madison County, not seasonally adjusted. Latest value shown on 4 October 2026 was June 2026.

612.title: [330] Unemployment Rate in Cullman County, AL (ALCULL0URN), monthly
612.text: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED); source U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. FRED's copy of the BLS monthly series for Cullman County, not seasonally adjusted. Latest value shown was June 2026.

613.title: [331] SNAP Benefits Recipients in Madison County, AL (CBR01089ALA647NCEN)
613.text: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED); source U.S. Census Bureau, Small Area Income and Poverty Estimates. Annual count of SNAP participants in Madison County as used by the Census Bureau's poverty-estimates program; latest year 2023.

614.title: [332] SNAP Benefits Recipients in Cullman County, AL (CBR01043ALA647NCEN)
614.text: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED); source U.S. Census Bureau, Small Area Income and Poverty Estimates. Annual count of SNAP participants in Cullman County; latest year 2023.

615.title: [333] SSI Recipients by State and County, 2024: Alabama (Table 3)
615.text: Social Security Administration, Office of Retirement and Disability Policy. SSA's county table of Supplemental Security Income recipients in December 2024, by eligibility category and age, with monthly payment amounts.

616.title: [334] QuickFacts: Cullman County, Alabama
616.text: U.S. Census Bureau. Census QuickFacts (V2025; ACS 2020-2024) for Cullman County: rent, home value, ownership, income, poverty, education, insurance, broadband and commute. The page was requested for both counties but the reader returned Cullman only.

617.title: [335] IPS WORKS ALABAMA: The Alabama Department of Mental Health Expands Program to Support Employment for Individuals with Serious Mental Illness
617.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH's release naming the five community mental health centers that offer Individual Placement and Support supported employment. None is in north Alabama.

618.title: [336] ADRS Office Locations (REV 12-2025)
618.text: Alabama Department of Rehabilitation Services. The state rehabilitation agency's office list. The Huntsville vocational rehabilitation office serves Jackson and Madison counties; Cullman County is served from the Decatur office.

619.title: [337] HAPPI Health (home page)
619.text: HAPPI Health (Central North Alabama Health Services). The health center's home page: four Huntsville sites, service lines including behavioral health, a sliding fee scale, and the figures '13k+' patients and 16 years.

620.title: [338] Behavioral Health
620.text: HAPPI Health (Central North Alabama Health Services). HAPPI Health's behavioral health page: therapy, evaluations, substance use assessments and crisis intervention by counselors and clinical social workers, with same-day appointments. No psychiatry or medication management is named.

621.title: [339] Thrive Alabama (home page)
621.text: Thrive Alabama. Thrive Alabama's site: clinic addresses in Huntsville, Florence and Albertville and its service list (primary care, pediatrics, HIV care, substance use treatment, pharmacy). The site text read does not state whether it is a federally qualified health center.

622.title: [340] Community Free Clinic of Huntsville (home and About pages)
622.text: Community Free Clinic. The free clinic's own description: care since 1999 for Madison County residents with no insurance, Medicaid or Medicare, with volunteer clinicians and an on-site dispensary. No mental health or dental service and no patient numbers are stated.

623.title: [341] Good Samaritan Health Clinic of Cullman (home page)
623.text: Good Samaritan Health Clinic of Cullman, Inc.. The free clinic's home page: who it serves (uninsured adults aged 19 to 65), its services including mental health counseling, and its address.

624.title: [342] Services
624.text: Good Samaritan Health Clinic of Cullman, Inc.. The clinic's services page: counseling through a memorial fund partnership, free medications through patient assistance, volunteer dental extractions.

625.title: [343] Madison County Health Department
625.text: Alabama Department of Public Health. ADPH's page for the Madison County Health Department: Northern District, WIC, environmental, home care and clinical services. No behavioral health service is listed.

626.title: [344] State Report Card: County, City school systems report highest grades in system histories
626.text: The Cullman Tribune. Tribune report of the 2024-25 state report cards: Cullman County Schools 91, Cullman City Schools 96, with the city system's graduation, readiness and absenteeism rates.

627.title: [345] Cullman school systems earn top ratings on state issued report cards
627.text: The Cullman Times. Cullman Times report giving Cullman County Schools' graduation, college-and-career readiness and absenteeism rates from the 2024-25 report card.

628.title: [346] Report cards for Huntsville and Madison County schools
628.text: WAFF 48. WAFF report of the 2024-25 state report card scores for Madison County Schools (91), Huntsville City Schools (89) and Alabama (87). No graduation rates.

629.title: [347] Area Agency on Aging
629.text: Top of Alabama Regional Council of Governments (TARCOG). TARCOG's Area Agency on Aging page: its state designation for a five-county area, its service list, and a list of what seniors need most that includes mental health services.

630.title: [348] Basic Needs Initiatives & Partners
630.text: United Way of Cullman County. United Way of Cullman County's basic-needs page: 2-1-1, a Food Insecurity Task Force, the disaster coalition's members, the Commission on Aging's senior centers and meals, and the food bank at Cullman Caring for Kids.

631.title: [349] CARTS ridership climbs 29% in July
631.text: The Cullman Tribune. Tribune report of CARTS's July 2026 figures: ridership up 29 percent, 190 rides per operating day, more than 46,000 miles.

632.title: [350] Social Services in Madison County: Homelessness, Housing, and Shelter Resources
632.text: Huntsville-Madison County Public Library. The public library's maintained list of 16 housing and homelessness resources in Madison County, with descriptions and phone numbers; last updated 9 September 2026.

633.title: [351] Social Services in Madison County: Food Resources
633.text: Huntsville-Madison County Public Library. The library's list of 26 food resources in Madison County, many of them congregations: FOODline, HAP pantries, Manna House, Rose of Sharon Soup Kitchen, the Salvation Army and others.

634.title: [352] The Link is asking for your help: 'Cullman has always shown up'
634.text: The Cullman Tribune. Tribune report, on the eve of the November 2025 SNAP suspension, quoting The Link's director: its pantry serves 800 households a month and over $1 million in SNAP benefits is distributed in the county each month.

635.title: [353] Where neighbors become family: The Link joins Alabama Network of Family Resource Centers
635.text: The Cullman Tribune. Press report that The Link became Alabama's 28th accredited Family Resource Center, with its director's account of the needs it handles. It dates The Link's service to 2013.

636.title: [354] Madison County, AL - profile
636.text: Data USA (Deloitte / Datawheel; American Community Survey data). An aggregator's county profile presenting Census Bureau survey estimates of health coverage by type for 2024 with the change from 2023. The page as read does not name the underlying table.

637.title: [355] Cullman County, AL - profile
637.text: Data USA (Deloitte / Datawheel; American Community Survey data). The same aggregator's profile for Cullman County: health coverage by type for 2024 and the change in the uninsured share from 2023.

638.title: [356] QuickFacts: Madison County, Alabama
638.text: U.S. Census Bureau. Census QuickFacts (vintage 2025). The reader returned only the Madison County column: population, veterans, share aged 65 and over, share under 65 without health insurance, poverty and median household income. QuickFacts does not print the data year of the uninsured figure in the row label.

639.title: [357] QuickFacts: Cullman County, Alabama
639.text: U.S. Census Bureau. The same QuickFacts table opened with Cullman first; the reader returned only the Cullman County column. It gives population, veterans, share aged 65 and over and share under 65 without health insurance.

640.title: [358] Demographic Breakdown of Medicaid Eligibles (Eligibility by County, April 2026)
640.text: Alabama Medicaid Agency. Alabama Medicaid's monthly county table of Medicaid eligibles, comparing April 2025 with April 2026 (file dated 10 June 2026 by its name). It gives one count per county and statewide breakdowns by age, race, gender and dual Medicare-Medicaid status. As read it carries no footnote defining 'eligibles' or saying whether ALL Kids (CHIP) is included.

641.title: [359] Medicare Monthly Enrollment - Madison County, Alabama, 2025 (data API)
641.text: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services. CMS's official Medicare enrollment dataset, queried for Madison County (FIPS 01089) for 2025. It returns one yearly and twelve monthly records with total beneficiaries, Original Medicare, Medicare Advantage and other health plans, aged and disabled, and dual-eligible counts. The dataset's catalog entry gives 21 May 2026 as its last update.

642.title: [360] Medicare Monthly Enrollment - Cullman County, Alabama, 2025 (data API)
642.text: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services. The same CMS dataset queried for Cullman County (FIPS 01043) for 2025: yearly and monthly counts of Medicare beneficiaries by plan type, entitlement and dual status.

643.title: [361] CHIP Enrollment By County, July 2026
643.text: Alabama Department of Public Health (ALL Kids). ADPH's monthly county table of Children's Health Insurance Program enrollment, split into ALL Kids (146-317 percent of poverty) and MCHIP, the Medicaid/CHIP expansion group (100-145 percent). It gives Cullman 4,757, Madison 12,741 and a state total of 196,836 for July 2026.

644.title: [362] ALL Kids / CHIP enrollment by county, July 2025
644.text: Alabama Department of Public Health. ADPH's monthly county table of children enrolled in ALL Kids and in the Medicaid/CHIP expansion group, for July 2025 - one year before the table read in the first sweep.

645.title: [363] National ACA disenrollments could impact trust in programs, overall Alabama state health
645.text: Alabama Reflector (by Anna Barrett). Report on marketplace enrollment after the enhanced tax credits expired at the end of 2025, with the number of Alabamians who left the marketplace. Statewide only.

646.title: [364] Local health care providers brace for end of subsidies
646.text: The Decatur Daily. Regional newspaper report on what the expiry of enhanced marketplace subsidies would mean for north Alabama providers. It carries Huntsville Hospital Health System's projection of $10-15 million more uncompensated care in 2026, current uncompensated-care figures for the Decatur and Athens hospitals, and KFF's statewide coverage-loss estimate. Projections made before the subsidies expired.

647.title: [365] 2026 Marketplace Open Enrollment Period Public Use Files
647.text: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services. CMS's index of 2026 open-enrollment public use files. It confirms that a county-level file exists for the 30 HealthCare.gov states, covering plan selections, premiums and financial assistance for the period 1 November 2025 to 15 January 2026. The file itself is a ZIP archive and could not be read, so no county figure is reported here.

648.title: [366] The Economic Impact of Expanding Medicaid in Alabama
648.text: Public Affairs Research Council of Alabama (with Jacksonville State and Samford universities). PARCA's 2022 economic analysis of Medicaid expansion. It estimates a statewide expansion population of 283,636 and, as read, gives no county-level estimates. Used here to document the absence of a county coverage-gap figure.

649.title: [367] Alabama Administrative Code chapter 560-X-47, Rehabilitative Services
649.text: Alabama Medicaid Agency (Alabama Administrative Code). Alabama Medicaid's rehabilitative-services rules (statewide reference 49). A mental-health provider must be certified by ADMH as a 310-board community mental health center; payment is a statewide maximum for each procedure code.

650.title: [368] Alabama Coordinated Health Network - Regional Contacts for Providers
650.text: Alabama Medicaid Agency. Alabama Medicaid's list of the seven ACHN regions with the network entity, telephone numbers and counties of each (file dated 16 April 2026 by its name). It places Cullman and Madison in the Northeast region, run by North Alabama Community Care, with Jackson, Limestone, Marshall and Morgan.

651.title: [369] Alabama Administrative Code chapter 560-X-41, Psychiatric Treatment Facilities
651.text: Alabama Medicaid Agency (Alabama Administrative Code). Alabama Medicaid's rules for inpatient psychiatric services for recipients under 21, in enrolled psychiatric hospitals and accredited psychiatric residential treatment facilities, with a required certification of need for admission. The chapter is confined to people under 21.

652.title: [370] Alabama Section 1115 Institutions for Mental Disease Waiver for Serious Mental Illness - CMS letter and special terms and conditions
652.text: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services. The terms of Alabama's serious-mental-illness waiver (statewide reference 97), approved 20 May 2022 to 19 May 2027. Federal payment is limited to institutions for mental disease in Baldwin and Mobile counties, for enrollees aged 21-64, though enrollees from any county may use them. No north Alabama facility is named.

653.title: [371] Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics (CCBHCs) Contract Billing Manual, version 2
653.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. ADMH's CCBHC billing manual, version 2, effective 1 April 2026 (statewide reference 105). It defines the PPS-1 daily payment and, as read, deals only with Medicaid billing: for people not on Medicaid it requires only that claims be kept and available on request.

654.title: [372] Prospective Payment System Re-base Schedule (memorandum to Alabama certified CCBHCs)
654.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health, Office of CCBHC. Memorandum of 9 July 2026 (statewide reference 289). Demonstration years run 1 July to 30 June; cost reports are due by 30 September; Alabama Medicaid sets the final rate; rates are re-based after the second demonstration year and every three years thereafter, and trended by the Medicare Economic Index in other years. It names no clinic.

655.title: [373] Alabama CCBHC Provider Manual, Version 4 (Q3 2026)
655.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. The current edition of the state's CCBHC manual, dated 1 July 2026. The reader returned the ability-to-pay rule, the 51 percent rule for designated collaborating organizations, the military-culture training rule and the annual review of care coordination agreements, but not the sliding-fee mechanics or the list of required partners.

656.title: [374] Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics (Office of CCBHC page)
656.text: Alabama Department of Mental Health. Home page of ADMH's Office of CCBHC, read 4 October 2026. It states the rule that a CCBHC must serve anyone regardless of residence, ability to pay or age, and that the nine services may be delivered directly or through a designated collaborating organization. It links the third-quarter 2026 manuals, the PPS re-base schedule and a PPS-1 rate estimator.

657.title: [375] Alabama mental health centers receive more than $8 million in rural health grants
657.text: Alabama Political Reporter. News report (statewide reference 29) on first-round Rural Health Transformation grants. It says WellStone receives $86,660 for tablets in Cullman County schools and names the six centers funded to pursue CCBHC certification, none of which is the center for Morgan, Lawrence and Limestone counties or the center for the Shoals.

658.title: [376] Competition in Health Insurance: A Comprehensive Study of U.S. Markets, 2025 Update
658.text: American Medical Association. The AMA's annual market-concentration study (statewide reference 100), enrollment as of 1 January 2024. Its Table A-1 gives each metropolitan area's concentration index and two largest commercial insurers: for the Huntsville metropolitan area, Blue Cross Blue Shield of Alabama 82 percent and Cigna 5 percent. Only the Alabama rows were read; the Medicare Advantage table was not returned.

659.title: [377] HH-Crestwood deal takes effect
659.text: Axios Huntsville. Short news item on the day after the acquisition closed. It says the deal was announced on 20 January 2026, that Crestwood keeps its name, and that the deal raised concerns about hospital competition and the cost of care. No price, bed count or regulatory action is given.

660.title: [378] Northwest Alabama Mental Health Center: 310 Board Plan 2025
660.text: Northwest Alabama Mental Health Center (posted by ADMH). Northwest's 310 board plan, the version ADMH's page links today (file uploaded 2025/01; header year 2025). It gives county populations, consumers served in 2023 by population group, the service list including mobile crisis in Marion and Winston, two 16-bed crisis residential programs and the 24-bed Walker Baptist unit it manages, and its goals. The reader returned selected quotations, not the full text.

661.title: [379] Crisis Services
661.text: Mountain Lakes Behavioral Healthcare. Mountain Lakes' page on its mobile crisis team: composition, 24/7/365 operation in Marshall and Jackson counties, phone numbers, and a statement that the team may coordinate inpatient admissions. It does not mention WellStone or the Huntsville crisis center.

662.title: [380] Who We Are
662.text: Mental Health Center of North Central Alabama, Inc.. The center's description of itself: a public non-profit serving Lawrence, Limestone and Morgan since 1967, with the number treated in 2023 and approximate staff count.

663.title: [381] Mental Health Center of North Central Alabama (home page)
663.text: Mental Health Center of North Central Alabama, Inc.. The center's home page, re-read on 4 October 2026 for any mention of the Decatur crisis residential unit: none. It lists six addresses, one of them the Decatur-Morgan Counseling Center at 4110 US Highway 31 S.

664.title: [382] Groundbreaking Ceremony Marks Start of Crisis Residential Unit in Decatur
664.text: Decatur-Morgan County Chamber of Commerce. Chamber of Commerce post reporting that the Mental Health Center of North Central Alabama broke ground on 10 December 2024 on a 16-bed crisis residential unit in Decatur for people committed to ADMH, with completion expected by October 2025, and quoting the center's CEO on travel distance. An announcement; no source confirming the unit opened was found.

665.title: [383] Job Opportunities
665.text: Mental Health Center of North Central Alabama, Inc.. The center's vacancies page. On 4 October 2026 it listed 'Crisis Residential Unit LPN - Morgan County' and 'Crisis Residential Unit RN - Morgan County' among 15 openings, with no dates.

666.title: [384] Services
666.text: Mental Health Center of North Central Alabama, Inc.. The center's service list (psychiatric and counseling services, school-based counseling, co-occurring substance use treatment, nursing-home services, housing programs) and its ACCESS appointment line. It lists no crisis program.

667.title: [385] CED Mental Health Center (home page)
667.text: CED Mental Health Center. CED's home page: serving northeast Alabama since 1974, three county offices (Center, Attalla, Fort Payne) with addresses, a 24-hour number and 'over 5,000 yearly consumers'.

668.title: [386] Adult Services
668.text: CED Mental Health Center. CED's adult services page: a 24-hour emergency call system, screening, outpatient, day treatment, case management and an ACT team. It names no mobile crisis team and does not mention the Huntsville crisis center.

669.title: [387] Etowah-Cherokee-DeKalb Mental Health Board, Inc. dba CED Mental Health Center: Strategic Plan Fiscal Years 2025-2027
669.text: CED Mental Health Center (posted by ADMH). CED's board-approved strategic plan (approved 13 November 2024), the version ADMH's 310-board page links today. It gives the three-county catchment's size and population, consumers served in fiscal year 2023-2024, the service list and a sentence on future CCBHC certification. The reader returned selected quotations, not the full text.

670.title: [388] Decatur Morgan West Behavioral Medical Center (member listing)
670.text: Alabama Hospital Association. The Alabama Hospital Association's directory entry for the psychiatric campus of Decatur Morgan Hospital: address, 64 authorized beds, adult and child/adolescent psychiatric services, and membership of the North Alabama Regional Hospital Council. Entry marked modified 4 February 2026.

671.title: [389] Mountain View Hospital (hospital directory entry)
671.text: Alabama Hospital Association. Directory entry for the freestanding psychiatric hospital in Gadsden (Etowah County): 68 authorized beds and its listed service lines. Entry marked modified 16 July 2024.

672.title: [390] Marshall Medical Center South (hospital directory entry)
672.text: Alabama Hospital Association. Directory entry for the Boaz campus of Marshall Medical Centers (Marshall County): 150 authorized beds in total and 'Psychiatric Adult Services' and 'Psychiatric Outpatient Services' among its service lines. No psychiatric bed count.

673.title: [391] Marshall Medical Center North (hospital directory entry)
673.text: Alabama Hospital Association. Hospital association entry for the Guntersville hospital: 90 authorized beds, adult and outpatient psychiatric services listed, no psychiatric bed count.

674.title: [392] Gadsden Regional Medical Center (hospital directory entry)
674.text: Alabama Hospital Association. Directory entry for the general hospital in Gadsden: 299 authorized beds in total and a service list that includes adult, geriatric and outpatient psychiatric services. No psychiatric bed count is given.

675.title: [393] Baptist Health Walker Hospital (hospital directory entry)
675.text: Alabama Hospital Association. Directory entry for the Jasper hospital formerly listed as Walker Baptist Medical Center: 267 authorized beds in total, with adult, geriatric and outpatient psychiatric services and detox, in the association's Birmingham Regional Council.

676.title: [394] A History of Caring (timeline)
676.text: HH Health (Huntsville Hospital Health System). HH Health's history timeline, with one-line entries recording when each affiliate hospital joined the system. The entry texts were returned verbatim, but the reader's assignment of years to entries was internally inconsistent, so no years are used from it.

677.title: [395] Dementia Resource Guide 2025 (list of Area Agencies on Aging)
677.text: Alabama Department of Senior Services (alabamaageline.gov). A state guide hosted on the Department of Senior Services' site (upload path 2025/08) that lists each Area Agency on Aging with the counties it serves. It supplies the county membership of TARCOG, NARCOG and the four other regional bodies that cover the 15 counties, after TARCOG's own pages could not be read.

678.title: [396] Ala. Admin. Code r. 560-X-37-.07, Alabama Coordinated Health Network Program
678.text: Alabama Medicaid Agency (rule text as published by Cornell Legal Information Institute). The Medicaid rule that defines the seven Alabama Coordinated Health Network regions by county, as amended effective 15 May 2025. It places the 15 counties in three different ACHN regions. Read on Cornell LII; the state's own PDF could not be opened.

679.title: [397] Alabama Mental Health Systems Report, v261003.1 (draft for review)
679.text: Little Orange Fish. The statewide companion to this report: Little Orange Fish's description of Alabama's mental health system in eight domains and four cross-sector sections, as checked claim by claim against its sources on 3 October 2026. It supplies the frame used here, the checked county data behind the maps and Appendix A, and the statement that a North Alabama regional edition on the same template was planned. It names Little Orange Fish as the backbone organization for the North Alabama Mental Health Coalition.

680.title: [398] CARTS (Cullman Area Rural Transportation System)
680.text: Cullman County Commission. The County's page for its rural demand-response transit: booking rule, distance-based fares, discounts and fleet.

681.title: [399] Wellstone to open only psychiatric in-patient wing for children in Madison County
681.text: WAFF 48. Local television report ahead of the pediatric unit. It carries the figure of about 800 children a year leaving Madison County for care, emergency-room waits of up to 24 hours and the distant places families travel to.

682.title: [400] Detention Center Information
682.text: Cullman County Sheriff's Office. The Sheriff's Office page for the Cullman County Detention Center, 1900 Beech Avenue SE, Cullman. It covers visiting, commissary and phones only; it gives no capacity, population, medical or mental-health information.

683.title: [401] National Children's Advocacy Center (home page)
683.text: National Children's Advocacy Center. Home page of the NCAC, which is based in Huntsville. It gives the organization's own estimate of how many Huntsville/Madison County residents its local services reach each year and links its local-services and impact pages.

684.title: [402] Social Services in Madison County: Mental Help: Counseling and Developmental Disabilities
684.text: Huntsville-Madison County Public Library. The library's list of eight mental health and developmental disability resources, including WellStone Emergency Services, NAMI Huntsville and the Madison County 310 Board.

685.title: [403] Madison City Schools overall rates 95 percent for Alabama State Report Card
685.text: The Madison Record. Local report of Madison City Schools' 2024-25 state report card score of 95 and the state average of 87.

686.title: [404] WellStone in need of nurses, other medical professionals
686.text: WHNT News 19. Local television report on WellStone's hiring needs after the move to 4020 Memorial Parkway SW in September 2022. The director of WellStone Emergency Services says admissions have tripled; the site listed more than 50 openings. No date found.

687.title: [405] State Supported Facility Analysis, FY 2022 Foundation Program
687.text: Alabama State Department of Education. ALSDE's FY2022 list of state-supported facilities whose resident children are educated by the local school system, with bed counts. It lists Neaves-Davis under Huntsville City and one residential facility under Madison County; no facility appears under Cullman County or Cullman City. Older than 2023.

688.title: [406] American Community Survey 5-Year Data Profiles, 2020-2024 (tables DP02, DP03, DP04 and DP05): census tracts in Madison and Cullman counties, the two counties and Alabama
688.text: U.S. Census Bureau. The Census Bureau's four data-profile tables from the 2020-2024 American Community Survey, retrieved from data.census.gov on 4 October 2026 for the 117 census tracts of Madison (95) and Cullman (22) counties, for the two counties and for Alabama. Eighteen published estimates were taken for each area with their published margins of error: population, age, race and ethnicity, veterans, median household income, poverty, unemployment, health insurance, disability, vehicles, broadband, education and renting. They are sample estimates for small areas, so many tract values have wide margins of error. One cell is suppressed by the Bureau (the rent-burden share for one Madison County tract). The values supply the tract layers of the regional map and are not used in the report's text.

689.title: [407] PLACES: Census Tract Data (GIS Friendly Format), 2025 release
689.text: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Division of Population Health. CDC's model-based estimates of health measures for every census tract in the country, 2025 release, retrieved from data.cdc.gov on 4 October 2026 for the 117 tracts of Madison and Cullman counties. The dataset's own description says the estimates are model-based and draw on the 2023 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (2022 for five measures), 2020 census population counts and American Community Survey estimates. Ten crude-prevalence measures for adults were taken: depression, frequent mental distress, loneliness, lack of social and emotional support, food insecurity, housing insecurity, lack of reliable transportation, no health insurance at ages 18 to 64, binge drinking, and fair or poor self-rated health. They are modeled values, not counts or survey results for each tract. They supply tract layers of the regional map and are not used in the report's text.

690.title: Little Orange Fish
690.text: Little Orange Fish — The Huntsville organization for which this report was prepared, and the publisher of the statewide companion report.

691.title: North Alabama Mental Health Coalition
691.text: North Alabama Mental Health Coalition — A Huntsville-area coalition of mental health stakeholders, formed in 2015 by a committee of the Society of St. Vincent de Paul.

692.title: WellStone (WellStone, Inc.)
692.text: WellStone · WellStone, Inc. · WellStone Behavioral Health · Mental Health Center of Madison County · Cullman Area Mental Health Authority · Cullman Area Mental Health · Cullman's mental health authority — The nonprofit community mental health center for Madison and Cullman counties. It also runs the Huntsville crisis center, a 988 call center and a pediatric crisis unit.

693.title: Community mental health center
693.text: community mental health center · community mental health centers · mental health center · mental health centers — One of the regional organizations that deliver public outpatient mental health care in Alabama. WellStone is the center for Madison and Cullman counties.

694.title: Catchment
694.text: catchment · crisis catchment — The set of counties a center is assigned to serve. It shows who is responsible for an area, not how far residents must travel or how much they use the center.

695.title: Crisis center (crisis diversion center)
695.text: crisis center · crisis centers · Crisis Diversion Centers · diversion center — A place open at all hours where a person in a mental health crisis can walk in or be brought by police or ambulance, as an alternative to an emergency room or jail.

696.title: WellStone Emergency Services
696.text: WellStone Emergency Services — WellStone's adult crisis center on Memorial Parkway in Huntsville. Its permanent building opened in September 2022, and the state assigns it fifteen counties.

697.title: Pediatric crisis unit (WellStone Pediatric Crisis Care)
697.text: pediatric crisis unit · pediatric unit · WellStone Pediatric Crisis Care — WellStone's 24-bed crisis unit for young people in Huntsville, opened in late September 2024 and listed by the state with the adult crisis center.

698.title: 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline
698.text: 988 — The national three-digit number for a mental health or suicide crisis. One of Alabama's four in-state call centers is at WellStone in Huntsville.

699.title: Probate court and probate judge
699.text: probate court · probate courts · probate judge — The county court that hears petitions for involuntary commitment in Alabama. Madison County's also runs an outpatient commitment program with WellStone.

700.title: Alabama Department of Mental Health (the Department)
700.text: Department of Mental Health · Alabama Department of Mental Health — The state agency for public mental health, substance use and developmental disability services. It certifies WellStone and names the counties each crisis center serves.

701.title: Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic (CCBHC)
701.text: Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic · Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics · CCBHC · certified clinic · clinic model — A clinic certified to provide a required set of mental health and substance use services to anyone who seeks care, and paid a daily rate by Medicaid. WellStone has been one since July 2024.

702.title: The core
702.text: the core — This report's name for Madison and Cullman counties, the two counties for which WellStone is the community mental health center.

703.title: The ring
703.text: the ring · ring counties · ring county — This report's name for the thirteen counties, beyond Madison and Cullman, that the state assigns to the Huntsville crisis center.

704.title: Service area (WellStone's three maps)
704.text: service area — The public record draws WellStone's service area three ways: two counties for routine care, fifteen for the crisis center, and a Region 1 that has three meanings of its own.

705.title: Region 1 (Region I)
705.text: Region 1 · Region I — A label with three different meanings in north Alabama: a mental illness services region, a 13-county Community Services office region and an 18-county police training region.

706.title: Crisis intervention training (Crisis Intervention Team, CIT)
706.text: crisis intervention training · crisis intervention team · crisis intervention officers · crisis intervention course · crisis intervention certification — Training that prepares police officers to respond to people in a mental health crisis. Huntsville Police is the training hub for an 18-county north Alabama region.

707.title: NAMI Alabama (and its local affiliates)
707.text: NAMI Alabama · NAMI · NAMI affiliate — The state organization of the National Alliance on Mental Illness and its local affiliate. Madison County has an affiliate; none is listed for Cullman County.

708.text: 2-1-1 — The telephone information and referral line for local help. Madison County's calls are answered in Huntsville and Cullman County's from Birmingham.

709.title: Continuum of Care (homelessness continuum)
709.text: homelessness continuums · Huntsville continuum · continuum of care — A regional body, recognized by the federal housing department, that plans the local response to homelessness and runs the yearly count. Madison and Cullman are in different ones.

710.title: County Health Rankings
710.text: County Health Rankings — A national publication of county health measures. This report uses its rural share, provider ratios, and suicide and overdose death rates for the fifteen counties.

711.title: 310 board (Act 310 of 1967)
711.text: 310 board · Act 310 · Act 310 of 1967 — A public corporation formed under Alabama's Act 310 of 1967 to contract with the Department of Mental Health. WellStone is the 310 board for mental illness in both counties.

712.title: National Children's Advocacy Center
712.text: National Children's Advocacy Center — A Huntsville center, opened in 1985, that brings prosecutors, police, child welfare staff and therapists together on child abuse cases and offers trauma therapy to children.

713.title: North Alabama Regional Hospital
713.text: North Alabama Regional Hospital — The state psychiatric hospital in Decatur, with 74 beds, whose closure the state announced in January 2015.

714.title: Diversion (and WellStone's jail diversion program)
714.text: diversion · diverted · jail diversion · jail diversion program — Steering a person away from jail or an emergency room and into care. It is the stated purpose of the crisis center, and no count of people diverted there has been published.

715.title: Stepping Up
715.text: Stepping Up · Stepping Up Initiative — A national initiative to reduce the number of people with mental illness in county jails. Madison and Cullman counties were both first-year Alabama sites in 2018–19.

716.title: Specialty courts (mental health, veterans and drug courts)
716.text: specialty docket · specialty dockets · mental health court · veterans court · drug court — Court dockets that put eligible defendants under supervised treatment in place of ordinary prosecution or jail. Both counties have set up mental health, veterans and drug court dockets.

717.title: Assisted outpatient treatment (outpatient commitment)
717.text: assisted outpatient treatment · outpatient commitment · outpatient commitment program · outpatient program — Court-ordered treatment in the community for a person who has been through the commitment process; in Madison County, run by the probate court with WellStone since 2020.

718.title: Civil commitment (involuntary commitment)
718.text: civil commitment · involuntary commitment · involuntary commitments · inpatient commitment · commitment petition · intent to commit · commitment · commitments — A court order requiring a person with mental illness to accept treatment. In Alabama the county probate court hears the petition; it is not a criminal matter.

719.title: House Bill 70 of 2022 (the revised commitment law)
719.text: House Bill 70 · commitment law · commitment bill — A 2022 Alabama law that added a ground for taking a person to a mental health facility and allowed courts to mandate outpatient care. It took effect in July 2022.

720.title: Mobile crisis team
720.text: mobile crisis · mobile crisis team · mobile crisis teams — Clinicians who travel to a person in crisis, at home or elsewhere in the community. WellStone runs adult and child teams in both Madison and Cullman counties.

721.title: Co-responder program
721.text: co-responder · co-responders · police co-responders — A police program in which a mental health clinician rides with an officer on calls involving a person in crisis. Huntsville's followed a council vote in May 2021.

722.title: Opioid settlement funds
722.text: opioid settlement · opioid settlement funds · opioid settlement money · settlement funds · settlement money · state opioid settlement fund — Money paid under legal settlements with companies that made and distributed opioids. The state, the counties and the cities each receive a share and decide how to spend it.

723.title: Detoxification (detox) and River Crossing
723.text: detox · detoxification · River Crossing · detox unit · detox program — Medically supervised withdrawal from alcohol or drugs, the first step of treatment. River Crossing is WellStone's 16-bed detox unit in Huntsville, opened on 24 June 2025.

724.title: Mountain Lakes Behavioral Healthcare
724.text: Mountain Lakes — The community mental health center for Jackson and Marshall counties, in the ring. It became the ring's first Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic in October 2025.

725.title: Huntsville Hospital Health System (Huntsville Hospital and Crestwood)
725.text: Huntsville Hospital · Huntsville Hospital Health System · Crestwood · Crestwood Medical Center — The hospital system owned by a public authority of the City of Huntsville. Since 31 March 2026 it has included Crestwood Medical Center as well as Huntsville Hospital.

726.title: Cullman Regional Medical Center
726.text: Cullman Regional Medical Center · Cullman Regional — Cullman County's hospital. It offers outpatient psychiatry and a behavioral health area in its emergency room, has no inpatient psychiatric unit, and publishes the county's needs assessment.

727.title: Days to first evaluation (wait for a first appointment)
727.text: first evaluation · days to first evaluation · initial evaluation — The number of days a new patient waits for an initial assessment. At WellStone it fell from 18 days in January 2025 to under one day in December 2025.

728.title: Group homes and supervised housing
728.text: group home · group homes · supervised housing — Places to live with staff support for adults with mental illness. WellStone names supervised housing as a priority, and a court official put the wait for a group home at 100 days or more.

729.title: Suicide rate (per 100,000)
729.text: suicide rate · suicide rates — Deaths by suicide per 100,000 residents, averaged over several years. County Health Rankings gives 15.3 for Madison County and 20.7 for Cullman County.

730.title: Drop-in center
730.text: drop-in center · drop-in centers — A free, voluntary community space for people with mental illness, outside clinical care. The state lists one in north Alabama, in Huntsville, and none in Cullman County.

731.title: Daily rate (prospective payment)
731.text: daily rate · single daily rate · clinic payment · clinic payment model — The fixed amount Medicaid pays a certified clinic for each day it gives a Medicaid enrollee a qualifying service, whatever the service. It is not paid for people outside Medicaid.

732.title: Medicaid (Alabama Medicaid Agency)
732.text: Medicaid · Alabama Medicaid · Alabama Medicaid Agency — The public health insurance program for low-income people, paid for jointly by the federal government and the state and run in Alabama by the Alabama Medicaid Agency.

733.title: Permanent supportive housing
733.text: permanent supportive housing · supportive housing — Long-term housing paired with support services, aimed at people leaving homelessness. In the Huntsville continuum it went from 334 beds in 2022 to 190 in 2025.

734.title: Form 990 (and single audits)
734.text: Form 990 · single-audit · public database — The Internal Revenue Service form on which a nonprofit reports its yearly revenue, expenses and assets. WellStone's latest on the public record is for the year ending September 2021.

735.title: Uncompensated care
735.text: uncompensated care — Care a provider delivers and is not paid for. WellStone reports nearly $3.4 million for fiscal year 2025; the Huntsville Hospital system's audit gives about $144.4 million.

736.title: Madison County 310 Board and Cullman County 310 Authority
736.text: Madison County 310 Board · Cullman County 310 Authority · intellectual disability · intellectual and developmental disability — The two local boards that coordinate services for people with intellectual disabilities, one in each county. They are separate from WellStone, the 310 board for mental illness.

737.title: Appropriation
737.text: appropriation · appropriations · outside agencies — Legal permission to spend a set amount of public money in a given year, granted by a legislature, council or commission. It is made one year at a time.

738.title: Fiscal year (FY)
738.text: fiscal year · fiscal years · FY2021 · FY2022 · FY2023 · FY2024 · FY2025 · FY2026 · FY2027 · FY2026–27 — A budget year, named for the year in which it ends. Alabama's runs from 1 October to 30 September, and WellStone's also ends in September.

739.title: WellStone's strategic plan (fiscal years 2026–2027)
739.text: strategic plan — The two-year plan WellStone files with the Department of Mental Health. The current one, signed on 18 November 2025, names its service area, people served and unmet needs.

740.title: Community health needs assessment
740.text: community health needs assessment · needs assessment — A periodic local study of a community's health needs. Cullman Regional publishes one for Cullman County; Madison County's nearest equivalent is a 2024 United Way assessment.

741.title: Be the Rock (capital campaign)
741.text: Be the Rock · capital campaign — WellStone's private fundraising campaign, launched in spring 2021, toward the cost of the crisis center and later the pediatric unit. Its page publishes no goal or total.

742.title: State evaluation office (Alabama Commission on the Evaluation of Services)
742.text: evaluation office — The state commission that evaluates whether state programs work. Its September 2025 report on the crisis centers found their monthly reporting inconsistent.

743.title: SAMHSA (Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration)
743.text: SAMHSA — The federal agency for mental health and addiction services, part of the Department of Health and Human Services. It made three grants to WellStone between fiscal years 2021 and 2025.

744.title: First Stop
744.text: First Stop — A Huntsville nonprofit serving homeless people. It received $810,000 of the city's first opioid settlement allocations and was named as one of the first stops for WellStone's mobile clinic.

745.title: Crisis Services of North Alabama
745.text: Crisis Services of North Alabama — An organization that runs a 24-hour crisis counseling line, a domestic violence shelter and sexual assault services, and manages 2-1-1 for Madison and five nearby counties.

746.title: Health insurance marketplace (and its tax credits)
746.text: marketplace · enhanced marketplace tax credits · marketplace tax credits · marketplace subsidies — The federal exchange where people without job-based coverage buy insurance, often with a subsidy. About 95,000 Alabamians left it after enhanced tax credits expired at the end of 2025.

747.title: Coverage gap (and Medicaid expansion)
747.text: coverage gap · expanded Medicaid · without expansion — Adults who earn too much for Alabama's Medicaid and too little for subsidized marketplace insurance. Alabama has not expanded Medicaid, and no county estimate of the gap was found.

748.title: Medicaid rehabilitative services
748.text: rehabilitative mental health services · rehabilitative services — The Medicaid benefit that pays for community mental health treatment. A mental health provider must be a center certified by the Department of Mental Health, which in these two counties is WellStone.

749.title: Institution for mental disease (and Alabama's federal waiver)
749.text: institutions for mental disease · federal waiver · waiver — Medicaid's term for a psychiatric facility of more than 16 beds, where it usually will not pay for adults aged 21 to 64. Alabama's waiver covers such stays only in Baldwin and Mobile counties.

750.title: ALL Kids (children's health insurance program)
750.text: ALL Kids · children's insurance program · children's health insurance — Alabama's Children's Health Insurance Program. With its Medicaid expansion group it covered 12,741 children in Madison County and 4,757 in Cullman County in July 2026.
